'''Saul Niborran'''{{fn|2}}  was a [[Saturn]]-born [[Lord General]] of the [[Imperial Army]], during the [[Great Crusade]] and [[Horus Heresy]], who was raised in the disciplines of the '''[[Saturnine Ordo]]s'''.{{fn|1}}{{fn|2a}}

===Biography===
By the time the Heresy began, Niborran was a veteran of war having served the Imperium for a 150 years. Due to the venerable General's skills, he was chosen by the [[Primarch]] [[Rogal Dorn]] to serve as [[High Primary Solar General]] in the '''Solar Command Staff''' as the [[Imperium]] prepared to defend [[Terra]] from Horus' treachery. He was known to have Dorn's complete confidence and during the Solar Command's meetings, Niborran would be chosen to speak the words, the Primarch could not. He was so favoured by Dorn, that the General was given command of several hundreds of millions of Imperial Army and Militia units on [[Terra]], when the [[Solar War]] began.{{fn|1}} Later as the [[Lion's Gate Spaceport]] fell, Niborran's colleague [[Colonel|Militant Colonel]] [[Clement Brohn]] panicked and bemoaned the state of the defenses. [[Jaghatai Khan]] flew into a rage and ordered that Brohn be expelled from the [[Bhab Bastion]]. When Niborran rose to Brohn's defense, he too was expelled by The Khan.{{Fn|2}} Burned out by the rigors of serving in the Bhab Bastion, and with the [[Siege of Terra]] going poorly for the Imperium, Nibboran and Brohn chose to place their names on the list for active duty. The War Courts assigned Niboran as zone command for the [[Eternity Wall Spaceport]].{{Fn|2a}}

Dorn regretted an officer of Niborran's experience and skill being treated in such a way, and when he discovered that the General had be reassigned to oversee defenses at the doomed Spaceport, dispatched his [[Huscarl]] [[Cadwalder]] to retrieve him before the complex was overrun. However despite knowing the truth, Niborran refused to leave and Cadwalder instead accompanied him as he oversaw the defenses alongside [[Shiban Khan]], [[Camba Diaz]], and [[Jenetia Krole]].{{Fn|2a}} When [[Angron]] delivered his order for the defenders of the Port to surrender, Niborran responded by having the gun-batteries of the facility open up on the Traitor Primarch.{{Fn|2b}} As the Port fell to a massive [[World Eaters]] assault, Niborran and Cadwalder died fighting off hordes of traitor Astartes together.{{Fn|2c}}

{{Character |Portal ={{EmperorsChildrenPortal}} |Name ={{PAGENAME}} |Image =SaulTarvitzArt.jpg |Caption ={{PAGENAME}}{{Fn|3}} |Title = |Homeworld = |Birth =c. [[M30]] |Active Period =[[M30]] - 005.[[M31]] |Death =005.[[M31]],
[[Isstvan III]] |Cause of Death =Killed by Traitor bombardment during the [[Battle of Istvaan III]] |Species =[[Human]] |Type =[[Astartes]] |Gender =Male |Relatives =[[Fulgrim]] ("Father" via [[gene-seed]]) |Occupation =[[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] of the [[Emperor's Children]] 10th Company{{Fn|7}} |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Imperium of Man]] **[[Emperor's Children]] |Notes = }} '''{{PAGENAME}}''' was a member of the [[Emperor's Children]] during the [[Great Crusade]].{{Fn|2b}} A line officer of the [[Emperor's Children]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]] of the [[Space Marines|Adeptus Astartes]], 10th Company [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] '''Saul Tarvitz''' personified all that was good and noble about his Legion. He had the respect of the troops under his command, and was happy with his position within the Legion, requiring only the opportunity to bring honour to his [[Primarch]] [[Fulgrim]] and the [[Emperor of Mankind]].{{Fn|2a}} He was not well loved by some of the more traditional members of the Legion's command staff, such as Lord Commander [[Eidolon (Emperor's Children)|Eidolon]].{{Fn|2b}} ===History=== In the 203rd year of the [[Great Crusade]], Tarvitz was part of the force that landed on the world of [[One Forty Twenty]], which would become known as [[Murder]]. The Emperor's Children had responded to a distress call sent by the [[Blood Angels]], who had landed on the planet and been decimated by the [[Megarachnids]] who lived there. Tarvitz was part of Eidolon's force that landed on the planet and was nearly wiped out as well.{{Fn|2a}} Tarvitz managed to hold back the Megarachnids and destroy some of their structures, keeping them at bay until further reinforcements from the [[Luna Wolves]] could arrive.{{Fn|2b}} The leader of the Luna Wolves spearhead was Captain [[Tarik Torgaddon]] of the [[2nd Company (Luna Wolves)|2nd Company]]. He and Tarvitz immediately bonded, and the two remained close friends. Tarvitz also became close with others of the Luna Wolves, finding them more like himself than most of his Battle-brothers in his own Legion.{{Fn|2c}} ====The Horus Heresy==== As the level of treachery within [[Horus]] and Fulgrim became apparent Tarvitz placed himself in the line of fire by willingly going to [[Isstvan III]]. There he and all suspected loyalist members would be betrayed by Horus. Horus ordered the bombardment of the planet, but Tarvitz, along with [[Garviel Loken]] and Tarik Torgaddon of the Luna Wolves, managed to turn the loyalist survivors into a cohesive fighting force. This "line officer" turned a planned slaughter into a full-scale battle, confounding the great [[Primarch]]s themselves. At the climax of the battle, Tarvitz fought [[Lucius (Emperor's Children)|Lucius]] in single combat after the swordsman had betrayed his own comrades. Tarvitz emerged as the victor in the duel, but Lucius managed to escape. When the traitors made their last assault upon the few remaining loyalists, Tarvitz fought to the last, but eventually fell in the bombardment of the planet, loyal to the very end.{{Fn|4}} ===Conflicting sources=== Tarvitz's rank as a captain of the Emperor's Children has been constant throughout the series. However, depending on the book, the company which he is attached to differs. In ''Horus Rising'', Tarvitz is only described as a captain{{Fn|2d}}, with no company assigned. In ''Galaxy In Flames'' and ''Flight of the Eisenstein'' he is mentioned consistently as the First Captain of the Emperor's Children.{{Fn|5}}{{Fn|6}} However, in ''Fulgrim'' that honour is assigned to [[Julius Kaesoron]], with Tarvitz assigned to the 10th Company.{{Fn|7}} ===Images=== [[Image:TarvitzMini.jpg|thumb|center|220px|Saul Tarvitz Miniature{{Fn|1}}]] ===Sources=== *{{Endn|1}}: [https://www.warhammer-community.com/2020/04/18/warhammer-preview-3-revenge-of-the-previewgw-homepage-post-1fw-homepage-post-1/ Warhammer Community: Warhammer Preview 3: Revenge of the Preview (posted 4/18/2020)] (last accessed 4/18/2020) *2: [[Horus Rising (Novel)]]: **{{Endn|2a}}: Part Two, Chapter Two **{{Endn|2b}}: Part Two, Chapter Four **{{Endn|2c}}: Part Two, Chapter Six **{{Endn|2d}}: ''Dramatis Personae'' *{{Endn|3}}: [[The Horus Heresy: Legions]] - Saul Tarvitz Card *{{Endn|4}}: [https://www.warhammer-community.com/2020/12/22/saul-tarvitz-the-first-loyalistgw-homepage-post-2fw-homepage-post-2/ Warhammer Community: Saul Tarvitz: The First Loyalist (posted 12/20/2022)] *{{Endn|5}}: [[Galaxy In Flames (Novel)]], ''Dramatis Personae'' *{{Endn|6}}: [[The Flight of the Eisenstein (Novel)]], ''Dramatis Personae'', Part One, Ch. Damocles and his company were present on [[Calth]] when the Ultramarines and [[Word Bearers]] were ordered by [[Horus]] to muster for the [[Ghaslakh Crusade]]. When the Word Bearers revealed [[Chaos|their true allegiance]] and attacked the Ultramarines, Damocles led his company in the resulting [[Battle of Calth]].{{Fn|1b}}

His company's sigil was a figure-eight serpent.{{Fn|1b}} He later founded the [[Iron Snakes]], a [[Successor Chapter]] of the Ultramarines, after the Heresy.{{Fn|2}}  The chapter's symbol was likewise a double-looped serpent, and one of its notable [[Tactical Squad]]s was named [[Damocles Squad|Damocles]]{{Fn|3}}.

The Wind of [[Nurgle]] |Homeworld = |Birth = |Active Period = |Death = |Cause of Death = |Species =[[Daemon]] |Type =[[Great Unclean One]] |Gender =Male |Relatives = |Occupation = |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Chaos]] **[[Nurgle]] |Notes = }} '''Scabeiathrax''' (known as '''Papa G’aap''', '''Lord of the Blighted Pit''', '''Maggotspore''' and '''The Wind of Nurgle''') is an ancient [[Great Unclean One]], who is a huge bloated sack of disease and contagion and is one of [[Nurgle]]’s most favoured [[Greater Daemon]]s.{{Fn|2}} He resides wallowing in one of Nurgle’s largest plague pits, called the [[Blighted Pit]], until he is called to plague the [[Real Space|corporeal universe]]. Wherever he treads he leaves a trail of disease, filth and corruption. He carries with him the ''[[Blade of Decay]]'', a crude rusting cleaver, imbued with the power to rapidly age and decay all it touches. Those who are hit by it find their wounds become instantly infected, and their flesh rotting away before their eyes.{{Fn|2}} As the [[Horus Heresy]] raged, Scabeiathrax was among the [[Greater Daemons]] summoned into [[Realspace]] by the [[Thousand Sons]], during the [[Battle for Terra]]{{Fn|1a}}. '''[[Colonel]] Schaeffer''' is an officer of the [[Imperial]] [[Commissariat]] and the commander of the [[13th Penal Legion]], also known as the "Last Chancers".

===History===
While most Imperial citizens, especially the rank-and-file of the [[Imperial Guard]], believe that [[Penal Legion]] troopers - often murderers, traitors, blasphemers, thieves, rapists and other assorted scum - should be executed for their crimes, Schaeffer is a firm believer of granting a "Last Chance" for his men to redeem themselves. He provides this chance by leading them into suicidal missions.{{Fn|3}}

Those "fortunate" enough to be offered recruitment into the 13th Legion often choose summary execution rather than serve under Schaeffer.{{Fn|1}}

During their mission on [[Armageddon]], Schaeffer revealed himself to be over three hundred years old, his life extended and his body reconstructed by [[Tech-priest]]s of the [[Inquisition]]. Among his injuries, he has had his eyes replaced (the ice-blue eyes that are his most distinguishing characteristic came from a tech-priest who sinned against the [[Machine God]]), his spine rebuilt after being crushed by a tank, and his arm replaced after it was shot off by a plasma bolt. He is also a master of close combat, either with his customary [[power sword]] and [[plasma pistol]], or hand-to-hand.

===Images===
[[Image:Colonel Schaeffer.jpg|thumb|center|Colonel Schaeffer miniature]]

===Trivia===
{{Trivia}}
In his foreword to [[The Last Chancers (Omnibus)]], [[Gav Thorpe]] explained that the concept for the 13th Legion began as a rescue team of Imperial Guard specialists, and for that reason, Schaeffer shares his name with Major "Dutch" Schaeffer, [[Wikipedia:Arnold Schwarzenegger|Arnold Schwarzenegger]]'s character in ''[[Wikipedia:Predator (film)|Predator]]''. Schaeffer was originally intended to be a [[Major]], but, after conferring with [[Andy Jones]], who suggested integrating the [[Penal Legion]]s and the premise of the earlier film ''[[Wikipedia:The Dirty Dozen|The Dirty Dozen]]'', Schaeffer was "promoted" to [[Colonel]] and the nature of his "team" changed.{{Fn|2}}

Sebastien Montante.wikitext:
{{ImperiumPortal}}
'''Sebastien Montante''' was [[Governor|Fabricator Marshal]] of [[Tarsis Ultra]] in late [[M41]], when the world came under attack by [[Hive Fleet Leviathan]]{{Fn|1b}}.

==History==
{{spoiler|source=Warriors of Ultramar (Novel)}}
As Fabricator Marshal, Montante was both planetary governor and a leading member of the Council of Industry which governed the capital city of [[Erebus (City)|Erebus]], and the nominal head of the planet's [[PDF]] forces{{Fn|1b}}.

Montante did not make a favorable first impression on the leaders of the [[Ultramarines]]' Fourth Company when they arrived on Tarsis Ultra, having arranged a sumptuous welcoming feast (which was brusquely cancelled) and expressing enthusiasm for the "adventure" of fighting a real war - apparently not grasping the horrors of fighting against [[Tyranid]]s{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|1b}}.

[[Space Marine Sergeant|Sergeant]] [[Learchus|Learchus Abantes]] was inclined to dismiss him as an empty-headed fool, but Montante managed to impress the [[Space Marines]] with his efficiency and dedication. By his own admission, he was not a soldier, but he was a first-class logistician and administrator. At his instruction, the PDF units began drilling as soon as word of the Tyranids' approach was received; food, water, medicine, and ammunition were stockpiled in caches under the city; and the arriving defenders from the Ultramarines, the [[Mortifactors]], and two [[Imperial Guard]] regiments, all found their requests for supplies being met promptly and in full. Thanks to Montante, the Imperial forces of Erebus were assured of having full ammunition and regular meals at all times, even during the worst of the invasion{{Fn|1b}}{{Fn|1c}}.

Montante was also instrumental on the Council of Industry, endorsing Learchus's instructions to demolish buildings standing between the city's defensive walls, in order to deny the incoming Tyranids cover{{Fn|1c}}.

When several members of the Council—including [[Simon Van Gelder]]—protested, Montante dissolved the Council and granted command of the city to [[Colonel]] [[Trymon Stagler]], one of the Imperial Guard commanders. Feeling that he had no further role to play as an administrator, he attempted to join the ranks of the PDF, declaring he needed to fight for his world. [[Uriel Ventris]] gently dissuaded him, instead drawing on Montante's knowledge of the planet's orbital defenses to devise a counterattack against the Tyranids{{Fn|1d}}.

Montante did take part in the final ground battle against the Tyranids. Although Learchus and several others had to save his life several times, none of them could doubt his personal bravery. He was killed fighting on the walls, by a volley of spikes fired by several [[Tyranid Warrior]]s{{Fn|1e}}.

After the battle was over, Montante's body was recovered and laid in honour in the Imperial Palace, and several [[Ecclesiarchy|Priests]] of Tarsis Ultra were petitioning for him to be made a [[List of Imperial Saints|saint]]. Privately, [[Pasanius Lysane]] reflected that Montante, a humble and selfless servant of his people, would have been much amused by the notion of being declared a saint{{Fn|1f}}.

==Background==
The character of Montante may have been inspired by [[wikipedia:Saint Sebastian|St. Sebastian]], a Catholic Saint who was martyred after being shot repeatedly with arrows.

Selena Agna.wikitext:
[[Image:Selena Agna.jpg|thumb|right|Canoness Selena Agna]]
[[Canoness]] '''Selena Agna''' of the [[Order of the Sacred Rose]] was the commander of the [[Sisters of Battle]] present on the Kaurava system during the Kaurava conflict.  Apart from fighting the xenos and heretics in the system, she also fought against the [[Blood Ravens]] and the [[Regiments of the Imperial Guard|252nd Conservator Regiment]], deeming the former a threat for not ceding authority to her forces, and the latter as corrupted, responsible in some way for the Warp Storm.

When the Sisters defeated all the other factions, they began a massive purge to rid the system of anything and anyone suspected of Heresy. The planets of the system became Monastery worlds with one ecclesiarchal citadel for each of the six major military orders of the Adepta Sororitas. Millions Sisters of Battle visited the system as a holy pilgrimage and reminder of their crusade in the Kaurava system and to gather for "Prayer and Preparation".

If the Sisters of Battle were defeated, the [[Saint Anais]] was killed in a hail of fire aimed at her head, while Selena Agna ordered ''"Sisters, we must go as Martyrs! We must go up in flames!"'' Selena Agna awaited the enemy approach, and when they closed on her, she activated a device that caused herself and the enemies near her to be burnt to death.

If defeated by the [[Space Marines]], all survivors were treated with the utmost deference, and were given swift medical aid and safe passage back to the Convent Sanctorum on [[Ophelia VII]] where they were at the mercy of the [[Inquisition]]. If defeated by the [[Imperial Guard]] forces, [[General]] [[Vance Stubbs]] remarked on his victory as a sign of the Emperor's will for their control over the system.

Her first name, Selena, is derivative of Selene, the moon goddess of Roman mythology; whereas her last name refers to the Hindu fire goddess - Agni - which is fitting, given the Sisters of Battle favour the use of flame-based weaponry in combat.

Selkar Fang.wikitext:
{{ImperialKnightsPortal}}
Sir '''Selkar Fang'''  was a [[Knight]] of [[Dominion (Knight World)|Dominion]]'s [[House Rau]] and piloted the [[Knight Armiger]] '''Jester'''{{Fn|1c}}.
==History==
He is the father{{Fn|1c}} of the [[Freeblade]]{{Fn|1a}} [[Linoleus Rakkan]], who Fang had through a political marriage with '''Baroness''' [[Hawthorn Astair-Rakkan]] of [[House Stryder]]. Hawthorn initially refused to marry Fang, due to his bloodline's low-status, but finally relented when House Rau would not offer a more suitable replacement. She felt they had only done so, in order to weaken House Stryder's chances of securing a [[High King|High Monarch]] candidate that would favor their House{{Fn|1c}}. Only nobles born from both Houses can become candidates on '''The Lists''' for High Monarch, but their initial standing depends on their parents' bloodlines{{Fn|1b}}. Because of Fang's low-status, Hawthorn knew their child would thus be on the low end of The Lists. This greatly angered her and as a result, Hawthorn had it written in a contract that their son, Linoleus, would have her last name and not Fang's. He agreed to this, but Sir Fang would later be declared a hero of [[Dominion (Knight World)|Dominion]], when he died saving High Monarch [[Lucien Yavarius-Khau]]'s life, during the [[Battle of Blazing Heaven]]. This greatly annoyed Hawthorn, however, as it meant she could no longer publicly speak ill of her husband again.{{Fn|1c}}

'''Sengur Khan''', also known as the '''Iron Khan''' due to his sustaining patchwork [[augmetic]]s, was the commander of the [[White Scars]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]]'s [[Brotherhood of the Black Axe]] and took part in the [[Chondax Campaign]].

Unfortunately though, they were among the Legion's forces that were accidentally left behind when the White Scars departed the System, following the [[Alpha Legion]]'s betrayal. For the next ten years on [[Irra Minor]], the Brotherhood had to survive constant attacks by not only the Alpha Legion, but also the [[Dark Mechanicum]] and [[Daemon]]s, while needing to scavenge old battlefields for supplies. Finally in 017.[[M31]], Sengur and the remnants of the Brotherhood were discovered by a [[Raven Guard]] patrol cruiser, which was seeking the trail of the [[Traitor Legion]] fleets fleeing their defeat in the [[Siege of Terra]]. When the Raven Guard made contact with the Khan and his Brotherhood however, the now highly paranoid warriors assumed they were a hostile force. This led to a brief skirmish to breakout between them, before the Raven Guard were able to convince the Brotherhood of their innocent intent. Afterwards the survival of Sengur and his eight surviving warriors reached the ears of the [[Primarch]] [[Rogal Dorn]], who invited the Brotherhood to [[Terra]] in order to receive honours for their valour. But the Khan and the Brotherhood instead chose to quietly return to their Homeworld [[Chogoris]], without fanfare.{{Fn|1}}

Sentor Jool.wikitext:
{{SpaceMarinesPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was the [[Chapter Master|Firstblade]] of the [[Knights of Blood (Chapter)|Knights of Blood]], when they aided [[Baal]] as it faced an [[Devastation of Baal|invasion]] by [[Hive Fleet Leviathan]].


==Biography==
By order of the [[Blood Angels]]' [[Chapter Master]], [[Dante]], the Knights of Blood were sent to defend [[Baal Primus]] - a task they did not object to, as the [[Flesh Tearers]] were also defending the moon. This was because the Knights of Blood felt a kindred spirit in the Flesh Tearers, as their two Chapters bore the strongest affliction for the [[Red Thirst]] and [[Black Rage]]. Sentor personally viewed the Flesh Tearers' [[Chapter Master]], [[Gabriel Seth]], as a triumphant figure of hope for the [[Sons of Sanguinius]], because he successfully fought to keep their bloodline's curses from damning or destroying his Chapter.{{Fn|1a}}  Seth, however, refused to fight beside Sentor's Chapter, due to the Knights of Blood's well known habit of wantonly killing [[human]]s, to feed on their blood. In the eyes of their brethren Chapters, the Knights of Blood had damned themselves by viewing humans as merely sheep to be devoured whenever they needed to keep the Red Thirst and Black Rage at bay. Santor did not deny this, but he explained that the Knights of Blood shared their [[Primarch|Primarch's]] curse of foresight and their visions showed them fighting beside the Flesh Tearers. They would not budge from this, no matter what objections Seth had. They nearly came to blows then, but Seth ultimately relented, as it would be foolhardy for the two Chapters to fight each other as Leviathan bore down on them. However, Seth firmly stated that while the Knights of Blood may fight near the Flesh Tearers, their Chapters would never fight together against the Hive Fleet. Sentor reluctantly agreed and the two left to ready their Chapters for war.{{Fn|1a}}

As Levithan invaded Baal Primus, Seth's declaration held true, until the Flesh Tearer determined that the Hive Fleet would soon claim the moon they had fought to save. With there being nothing their dwindling forces could do to defeat the Hive Fleet, Seth fought to Sentor's side and said their Chapters should aid in defending Baal from being consumed as well. Sentor at first resisted the idea, as he was angered by the fact that Seth had refused to allow their forces to fight together, but he quickly agreed and the remains of the two Chapters fought their way to an extraction point.{{Fn|1b}}  However, just as [[Thunderhawk]]s neared their position, the [[Bloodthirster]] [[Ka'Bandha]] appeared from the [[Warp]] and sent a shockwave of rage across Baal Primus's surface. This proved to be too much for the Knights of Blood, who had been struggling to keep their curses at bay during the battle, and as [[Daemon]]s of [[Khorne]] fought [[Tyranids]] around them, Sentor told Seth his Chapter could not leave. The Chapter Master then removed his helmet and showed Seth that he had been right, the Knights of Blood were truly damned. They had thought that, by freely feeding on blood, they would keep their curses in check, but in truth this accelerated their fall and mutated their appearances. The Knights of Blood now appeared similar to those bestial figures the [[Blood Angels]] kept imprisoned within the [[Tower of Amareo]] and only blood kept the Black Rage from claiming them. Because of this, they could not risk fighting beside other Chapters, for fear of their appearances being discovered. In truth, that was why Sentor had wanted to fight beside the Flesh Tearers, as they alone would understand his Chapter's constant struggle against their curses.{{Fn|1c}}

All that was now moot though, as with Ka'Bandha's appearance the Knights of Blood had fallen fully to the Red Thirst and Black Rage, and were no longer capable of hiding their secret shame. Sentor was among those who were barely able to control themselves, but he knew that if the other Sons of Sanguinius saw his Chapter now, the Knights of Blood would be hunted down and destroyed. He would not allow that to happen, nor would he allow Ka'Bandha to corrupt his Chapter into serving Khorne. Instead, the remaining Knights of Blood would sacrifice themselves in penitence for their actions and unleash their holy fury upon the approaching Daemons and Tyranids. Before they went to their deaths, Sentor asked Seth to remember them and to always strive to prevent the Flesh Tearers from damning themselves like his Chapter did. With that, Sentor then led the Knights of Blood in attacking their foes and by doing so, they allowed the Flesh Tearers still remaining in the extraction point, to escape into awaiting Thunderhawks.{{Fn|1c}}  As the Flesh Tearers reached Baal Primus's orbit, Sentor fought his way to Ka'Bandha and challenged the Bloodthirster that had doomed his Chapter. The [[Greater Daemon]] greeted Sentor and said that if the Chapter Master joined its forces, he would be given a lifetime of battle that would quench his thirst for blood. Sentor vehemently refused and then let loose a roar as he attacked the Bloodthirster, but he was no match for Ka'Bandha and was killed.{{Fn|1c}}

Separatist Tyrant.wikitext:
The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' was the name given to the ruler of the [[Imperium]] world [[Farhaj]] after he led it into rebellion.  Once word of his treachery reached the Imperium, its forces were sent to reclaim Farjaj and among them were the [[Knight]]s of [[House Draconis]].  The Knights would later clash with the {{PAGENAME}} and defeated him in battle.  Though Draconis' High King, [[Tolwyn Tan Draconis]], ordered that the {{PAGENAME}} was to be shown mercy, the Knight [[Markos Dar Draconis]] refused and beheaded the Tyrant; he stated afterwards that he considered the man a [[heretic]] beyond even the [[Emperor of Mankind|Emperor's]] forgiveness.  After his death, the Tyrant's forces were defeated and Farhaj was reclaimed by the Imperium.{{Fn|1}}

He was famous in that he often carried with him the glistening stomach sac of some unfortunate creature with protruding hollow antlers, on which he played like on the bagpipe, summoning such a terrible sounds that it exasperated even his fellow daemons. During the later years of the [[Plague Wars]], Septicus aided the Plague Guard{{Fn|1a}} in claiming the [[Ultramar]] world [[Iax]] for Nurgle{{Fn|1b}}. The Plague Guard then invaded [[Parmenio]] and later clashed with the Imperium forces led by [[Lord Commander]] [[Roboute Guilliman]]. During the battle, Septicus fought Guilliman, but his essence was destroyed by the [[Sword of the Emperor]] of the [[Lord Commander]].{{Fn|2}}{{Fn|3}}

Seraphicus.wikitext:
{{DarkAngelsPortal}}
[[File:DAChaplain.jpg|thumb|right|Interrogator-Chaplain Seraphicus{{Fn|1}}]]
'''Seraphicus''' is an [[Interrogator-Chaplain]] of the [[Dark Angels]]. He took part in the [[Battle for Bane's Landing]] in [[M41]], fighting alongside [[Space Marine Captain|Company Master]] [[Balthasar]],{{Fn|1}}

==Biography==

In 960.[[M41]] he took part in the [[Pandorax Campaign]]. During the campaign Seraphicus took part in the battle on the asteroid Malefus Murex, during which he removed the [[Gene-seed]] from the corpses of dead [[Black Legion|Black Legionaries]] so they could be brought to [[The Rock]] for testing, to confirm if any of [[The Fallen]] were among the dead.{{Fn|2}}

After the entire [[4th Company (Dark Angels)|Dark Angels 4th Company]] was wiped out on the [[Space Hulk]] Harbinger of Woe, with the exception of [[Space Marine Sergeant|Sergeant]] [[Arion]], Seraphicus went to see Arion on the [[Salvation]], and offered him a place in the [[Ravenwing]] as a Sergeant. Seraphicus commented on the fact that this is the second time Arion has been found as the sole survivor of a battle, speculating that perhaps the Emperor and the Lion had a plan for him.{{Fn|1c}}

In 999.[[M41]]{{Fn|3}} Seraphicus was present for the [[Battle for Bane's Landing]]. Though instead of going down to the planet, he remained on the [[Sword of Caliban]] to interrogate{{Fn|1a}} [[Kestalev Chyre]] of the [[Crimson Slaughter]]{{Fn|1b}}. After the traitor revealed that he knew Seraphicus' name, and stated that the Dark Angels knew about the [[Hellfire Stone]], Seraphicus left for his quarters to inform [[Balthasar]] that the enemy may know more about them, then they know about their enemy.{{Fn|1a}} He later continued the interrogation, and after asking who Kestalev kept talking to, as he seemed to be talking to no one, Kestalev then became possessed by a ghost of Balethu. The ghost then told Seraphicus about how they were slaughtered by the [[Crimson Sabres]], and then attached themselves to the space marines to torment them. It also revealed that the [[Crimson Slaughter]] thought the stone would get rid of the Balethu. The ghost then let Kestalev control his body again. After more physical torture Kestalev told Seraphicus that the Balethu were trying to summon a [[Daemon]].{{Fn|1d}} Seraphicus then tried to find out the Daemon's true name, but Kestalev revealed they didn't know it, only that the Daemon is called [[Haur'esh]]. When Seraphicus asked what the ritual to summon him was Kestalev died. Seraphicus, acting quickly, broke Kestalev's ribs with his [[Crozius]] and then cut open his body with his combat knife, exposing Kestalev's two hearts which were no longer beating. He then activated his Crozius, the electrical power restarting his hearts. Alive again, Kestalev finally revealed that the ritual required a blood sacrifice of a [[Space Marine]]. Seraphicus then quickly left the interrogation chamber{{Fn|1e}} and warned [[Balthasar]] about the blood sacrafice over Vox.{{Fn|1f}}

After the battle Seraphicus went down to the planet to deal with the dead, commending their souls, as well as retrieving their [[Gene-seed]] since they lacked an [[Apothecary]]. [[Balthasar]] planned to talk with Seraphicus after the battle about [[Turmiel]], and how he might have ostracised himself even more from the rest of the company.{{Fn|1g}}

Seraphus.wikitext:
{{DarkAngelsPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was the [[Space Marine Captain|Master]] of the [[Dark Angels]]' [[4th Company (Dark Angels)|Fourth Company]], who commanded a Lion's Blade strike force sent to secure the [[Calaphrax Cluster]].{{Fn|1a}}

==Biography==
[[Image:Seraphus.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Fourth Master {{PAGENAME}}]]
Seraphus was charged by [[Dark Angels Grand Master|Supreme Grand Master]] [[Azrael]] to lead a Lion's Blade strike force to the [[Calaphrax Cluster]], a region that had been cut off by [[warp-storm]]s for ten millennia, in order to ensure the secret of the [[Fallen]] was preserved. The strike force consisted of his own Fourth Company, elements of the [[Deathwing]] and [[Ravenwing]]{{Fn|1c}}, and [[Interrogator-Chaplain]] [[Altheous]], who departed to ascertain the loyalty of the [[Knight World]] [[Tintaroth]].{{Fn|1a}}

Initially deploying a single squad under [[Space Marine Sergeant|Sergeant]] Kalidius on a reconnaissance mission,{{fn|1b}} he deployed the full strike force via an orbital drop after the [[Iron Warriors]] launched an asteroid into the [[hive]], engaging the [[Chaos Space Marine]]s in the [[Second Battle of Exyrion]].{{Fn|1c}} He survived the battle, but feared the [[gene-seed]] of the fallen could not be recovered.{{Fn|2a}}

Sending Altheous after a [[Thunderhawk]] seen leaving Exyrion, Seraphus took the majority of the strike force to [[Quintus (Forest World)|Quintus]] to investigate reports of a [[xenos]] fleet.{{Fn|2a}} When the [[Harlequin]]s activated the fallen [[Craftworld]] [[Theminarae]] and awoke the [[Necron]] [[Tomb World|tomb]] below, Seraphus ordered [[Techmarine]] [[Larathiel (Techmarine)|Larathiel]] to attempt to overload the Craftworld's engines and destroy it while he led the Dark Angels in the [[Battle of Quintus]] against both xenos forces.{{Fn|2c}}

==Wargear==
Master Seraphus wears [[Mark VII|Mark VII Power Armour]]. He wields a large [[Power Sword]] and a [[Bolt Pistol]].{{Fn|2b}}

(Formerly) **[[Sons of Horus]] *[[Dark Empire]] |Notes = }} '''Serghar Targost''' was the [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] of the [[7th Company (Sons of Horus)|7th Company]] of the [[Luna Wolves]] [[Space Marine Legion]], as well as the lodge-master of the [[warrior-lodge]] that existed within the legion. He was blunt in appearance, with a scarred forehead.{{Fn|1b}} ===History=== Targost commissioned the mold for the lodge medallions from a [[remembrancer]] silversmith assigned to the ''[[Vengeful Spirit]]'', whom he killed shortly afterward to preserve the secrecy of the lodges.{{Fn|4}} Targost believed passionately in the role of the warrior-lodge, stating that as genetic constructs employed singularly for war, the [[Astartes]] needed a way to form and express their bonds of brotherhood in a way that wasn't constrained by the pressures of duty.{{Fn|1a}} Targost operated as the voice of the lodge, regulating and organising the meetings.{{Fn|1a}} In his role of lodge-master, he was instrumental in the decision to place the wounded [[Horus]] into the care of the [[Serpent Lodge]], thus ensuring Horus's damnation.{{Fn|2}} As a senior officer of the [[Sons of Horus]] and one who saw things from the [[Warmaster]]'s point of view, Targost co-commanded the initial Sons of Horus deployments against the loyalist marines upon [[Isstvan III]].{{Fn|3}} During the battle on [[Dwell]], Targhost suffered a catastrophic head injury that shattered his skull. Only the pressure of his helmet kept the ruination of his head together. The legion apothecaries managed to stitch his skull back together and he had plundered Salamanders drake-claws attached to the fasteners, giving him a far more terrifying appearance that precluded his ability to wear a helmet again. He led the ceremony that invested [[Ger Geraddon]]'s brain-dead body with the [[daemon]] [[Tormageddon]].{{Fn|6a}} Targost died when [[Rama Karayan]] shot him through the head before he could invest [[Proximo Tarchon]] with a [[daemon]] in the bowels of the ''[[Vengeful Spirit]]''. Moments after Targost's death, [[Samus]] possessed his body.{{Fn|6b}} He managed to kill [[Tubal Cayne]] before Tarchon destroyed Targost/Samus with his gladius.{{Fn|6c}} ===Sources=== {{Cite}} *1: [[Horus Rising (Novel)]] **{{Endn|1a}}: Part Two, Chapter Five, pgs. 284–287 **{{Endn|1b}}: Part One, Chapter Seven, pg. 143 *{{Endn|2}}: [[False Gods (Novel)]], Chapter Eleven, pg. 213 *{{Endn|3}}: [[Galaxy in Flames (Novel)]], Chapter Twelve, pg. 290 *{{Endn|4}}: [[Death of a Silversmith (Short Story)]] *{{Endn|5}}: [[Collected Visions]],{{Cite This}} *6: [[Vengeful Spirit (Novel)]] **{{Endn|6a}}: Chapter 6 **{{Endn|6b}}: Chapter 21 **{{Endn|6c}}: Chapter 22 {{DEFAULTSORT:Targost, Serghar}} [[Category:Characters (Horus Heresy)]] [[Category:Characters (Sons of Horus)]] [[Category:Characters (Deceased)]] [[de:Serghar Targost]] [[fr:Serghar Targost]]

Serivahn.wikitext:
{{SpaceMarinePortal}}
'''Serivahn''' is the [[Emperor's Spears]] [[Primaris Space Marine|Primaris]]{{Fn|1a}} [[Shipmaster]], of the 3rd [[Space Marine Company|Warhost]]'s [[Strike Cruiser]], ''[[Hex]]''.{{Fn|1b}}

However, his Primaris [[Gene-seed]] implantation failed in the Alpha and Beta phases, which caused Serivahn's body to become heavily disfigured, with misshaped limbs and left him in constant pain.{{Fn|1a}} This was largely due to the [[Great Rift]], whose creation left the Spear's Homeworld, [[Nemeton]], and the other worlds of [[Elara's Veil]], cut off and isolated from the wider [[Imperium]]. It was only due to the arrival of a small Imperial strike force that the Spears were able to gain access to the information needed to create Primaris, but unfortunately not the technology to safely do so.{{Fn|1c}} This led the Spears to a tragic journey of trial and error that caused the deaths of numerous [[Aspirants]]{{Fn|1a}} before Serivahn miraculously survived. Using what they learned from his procedure, the Spears were able to perfect their Primaris creation and Serivahn would became known as the '''First Primaris Spear''', though he thinks of himself as only the first to survive. However, because of his disfigurements, Serivahn was not capable of physically joining his Chapter in battle and instead became the Shipmaster of the Strike Cruiser ''Hex''.{{Fn|1c}} The [[Tech-Priests]] of [[Bellona (Moon)|Bellona]] proposed to replace all of Serivahn's crippled parts with [[bionics]], but he refused.{{Fn|2}} Despite his appearance though, Serivahn is treated as a true [[Space Marine]] by both the [[Battle Brothers]] of his Chapter{{Fn|1c}} and their [[Celestial Lions]] allies, who all have great respect for the Shipmaster.{{Fn|1d}}

Servalen.wikitext:
{{NecromundaPortal}}
'''Servalen''' is a [[Scrutinator-Primus]] of the [[Palanite Scrutinator]]s, the [[Palanite Enforcer]]s' elite investigative and interrogation unit.{{Fn|1a}}

==Biography==
[[Image:Servalen.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Servalen and the [[Cyber-Mastiff]] [[KB-88]]{{Fn|1b}}]]
She has dismantled more criminal organizations and [[cult]]s than anyone else in recent memory. Her exceptional success has earned her the Provost Marshal's personal seal, granting her unrestricted access across [[Necromunda (planet)|Necromunda]].{{Fn|1a}}

Despite her unassuming physical presence, her unnerving aura induces extreme anxiety in those around her, due to her nature as a [[Blank|psychic null]], or pariah, which repels living beings. Servalen's sharp mind and relentless approach, combined with her disturbing presence, make her a formidable opponent. For added protection, she is accompanied by [[KB-88]], a Palanite pattern [[Hardcase Cyber-Mastiff]], which ensures her safety.{{Fn|1a}}

Setekh (Phaeron).wikitext:
{{NecronPortal}}
'''Setekh''' was the [[Necron]] [[Cryptek|Chronomancer]] and [[Phaeron]] of the [[Hyksos Dynasty]] and enemy of [[Ahzek Ahriman]].{{Fn|1a}}

==History==
In the ancient past, Setekh and the rest of his Dynasty engaged in dangerous temporal manipulations, culminating in the device dubbed the [[Key of Infinity]]. As a result, the [[Triarch]] sealed them away.{{Fn|1a}} However he is inadvertently reawakened by [[Ahriman]] and his cabal in [[M41]] as part of his quest to cure his [[Legion]] of the [[Pyrodomon]] affliction.{{Fn|1b}} Setekh initially seems to agree to help Ahriman discover the Key of Infinity in the [[Webway]] to defeat the Pyrodomon, but this was a ruse to allow the Necron Overlord to change the past himself. In the ensuing struggle, Ahriman seemingly kills Setekh but he is able to reawaken in a new body.{{Fn|1c}} 

Ahriman and Setekh subsequently both enter the Key, traveling back into the past. However the process begins to inflict Setekh and his followers with the [[Flayer Virus]], driving him to madness.{{Fn|2a}} In a renewed struggle with Ahriman's cabal in the past, Setekh and the Sorcerer are once again able to enter the Key of Infinity. However Ahriman uses his mastery of the Key's techniques to have Setekh completely consumed by the Flayer Virus and trapped within his own arcane device. In the new timeline created by the Key, Setekh does not exist.{{Fn|2c}}

(Formerly) ***[[2nd Company (Ultramarines)|2nd Company]] |Notes = }} '''{{PAGENAME}}'''{{Fn|1}} is the former [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] of the [[Ultramarines 2nd Company]].{{Fn|2}} ===Biography=== Acheran was originally an officer serving under [[Cato Sicarius]] in the 2nd Company. However, he became the Captain of the Company after Sicarius was lost to the [[Warp]] early in the [[Indomitus Crusade]], due to the formation of the [[Great Rift]].{{Fn|2}} ====War of Beasts==== One of his notable actions was leading the attack on the [[Black Legion]] held world of [[Nemendghast]], during the [[War of Beasts]]. Despite being badly outnumbered by the [[Black Legion]] forces during the [[Nemendghast Raid]], Acheran refused to leave and instead ordered an attack to destroy the world's Daemonic factories.{{Fn|2}} The orbiting [[Chaos]] fleet soon became alerted to Acheran's attack and as it began moving to aid [[Nemendghast]], the crew of the Captain's [[Strike Cruiser]] ''[[Carpatia]]'' warned Acheran of the fleet. The Captain then immediately led the remnants of his forces in a final attack that destroyed the [[Daemon]] factories, but by then they were swarmed by the [[Black Legion]]. Acheran knew they could not break free from the [[Traitor]]s and instead ordered the [[Vanguard Librarian]] [[Maltis]], to escape and bring word of what had happened to [[Chapter Master]] [[Calgar]]. Maltis successfully returned to the ''Carpatia'', which then escaped to [[Vigilus]].{{Fn|2}} ====Fourth Tyranic War==== Acheran would survive his battle on [[Nemendghast]] though, and later took part in the [[Fourth Tyrannic War]]. During the affair surrounding [[Project Aurora]], the [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] reincorporated [[Demetrian Titus]] as a [[Space Marine Lieutenant|Lieutenant]] into the [[2nd Company (Ultramarines)|2nd Company]], while it defended the [[Recidious System]] from [[Tyranids]]. However, Acheran still had some suspicions of Titus, due to his history as a [[Deathwatch Blackshield]] and detainment by the [[Inquisition]].{{Fn|3a}} The [[Thousand Sons]] later invaded the [[System]] as well and the 2nd fought the [[Traitor Legion]], under their [[Chapter Master]] [[Marneus Calgar]]'s command, on the Recidious [[moon]], [[Demerium]]. The [[Ultramarines]] emerged vicarious over the Thousand Sons and Acheran later congratulated Titus for his efforts in defending the the System after the battle.{{Fn|3b}} Sometime later, the [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] led a strike force to [[Trygg (World)|Trygg]] to investigate the disappearance of a [[Munitorum]] survey vessel. This was revealed to have been done by a [[Genestealer Cult]] and the Captain's forces were destroyed while defending the infested [[Hive World]]. Their sacrifice though, greatly reduced the spread of the Cult's rebellion and allowed Trygg to be saved by [[Imperial]] reinforcements. [[Demetrian Titus|Titus]] would then be selected to succeed Acheran as Captain of the [[Ultramarines]]' 2nd Company.{{Fn|5}} ===Images=== PrimarisCaptain.jpg|Captain Acheran in [[Gravis Armour]]{{fn|4}} AcheranMini.jpg||Captain Acheran in [[Phobos Armour]] ===Sources=== *{{Endn|1}}: [[Kill Team: Elites]], pg. 126 - ''Conquerors of the Killzones'' *{{Endn|2}}: [[Shadowspear]] campaign book, pgs. 6–9 *{{Endn|3}}: [[Space Marine II]] **{{Endn|3a}}: Mission 2, Severance **{{Endn|3b}}: Mission 5, Dawn's Descent *{{Endn|4}}: [[Codex: Space Marines (8th Edition, 2nd Codex)]], pg. 107 *{{Endn|5}}: [https://archive.ph/PTMA4 Warhammer Community: 500 Worlds – How did Titus become Captain of the Second Company (again)?] ''(Saved archive page, dated 11 November 2025, last accessed 11 November 2025, original link: https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-gb/articles/2uwxtd2k/500-worlds-how-did-titus-become-captain-of-the-second-company-again/)'' {{DEFAULTSORT:Acheran, Sevastus}} [[Category:Characters (Ultramarines)]] [[Category:Characters (Tyrannic Wars)]] [[Category:Characters (Deceased)]]

(former){{Fn|2}} *[[Chaos Lord|Lord]] of the [[Crimson Slaughter]]{{Fn|2}} |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Chaos]] **[[Crimson Slaughter]] |Notes = }} '''Sevastus Kranon''', also known as '''Kranon the Relentless''', is the former [[Chapter Master]] of the [[Crimson Sabres]] and current [[Chaos Lord]] of the [[Crimson Slaughter]] [[Chaos Space Marine]]s. ===History=== [[Image:KranonArt.jpg|thumb|right|280px|Kranon the Relentless]] Kranon was known to be militant and brutal even in his service to the [[Emperor]]. Upon leading his warband into self-imposed exile in the [[Eye of Terror]], Sevastus was corrupted by the powers of [[Chaos]]. Renaming himself Kranon the Relentless, he has driven himself to commit more and more bloody and vile acts in an attempt to silent the maddening voices that plague him, a result of a curse from [[Khorne]].{{Fn|2}} Kranon would later lead the Crimson Slaughter to [[Bane's Landing]] in search of the [[Hellfire Stone]], an artefact that would supposedly end his curse although the voices denied that it was possible. During the battle he claimed the lives of several [[Dark Angels]] and took the [[Ravenwing]] [[Space Marine Sergeant|Sergeant]] [[Arion]] prisoner for use in the ritual. However, Arion's suicide thwarted his plan and he was forced to retreat.{{Fn|3}} The Dark Angel [[Librarian]] [[Turmiel]] would predict that over the course of the next three years, Kranon would join forces with a much more powerful Chaos Lord and would be cornered on a moon in [[Tau]] space. The combined efforts of the Dark Angels and [[Space Wolves]] forced him into battle with [[Company Master]] [[Balthasar]] for the third time, having met and fought him twice before and escaped through [[teleporter]] both times. During the third confrontation, Kranon finally met his end, and his head was taken back to the [[Battle Barge]] ''[[Angel of Retribution]]'' by Balthasar in an iron box.{{Fn|3}} This has not yet come to pass, and somehow Kranon survived. Following the Battle of Bane's Landing, Kranon would suspect that he and his chapter were being used by an unknown power. This power would turn out to be the Lord of Change, [[Tzax’lan-tar]], who had been possessing the body of the former [[Chief Librarian]] [[Mannon]]. Kranon would pursue Mannon deep into the Eye of Terror, to a world called [[Mymidrax]]. There he would cut off the daemon's arm before it retreated yet again.{{Fn|4}} Currently, he leads at the forefront of one of the many speartips of the [[13th Black Crusade]]{{Fn|4}}, most notably in the [[Diamor Campaign]]{{Fn|5}} and during the attack on [[Cadia]].{{Fn|6}} ===Images=== [[Image:Kranon.jpg|thumb|center|220px|Kranon as Lord of the Crimson Slaughter{{Fn|2}}]] ===Related Articles=== *[[List of Chapter Masters]] *[[List of Chaos Lords]] *[[Mortis Metalikus]] ===Sources=== *{{Endn|1}}: [[White Dwarf 392]], pgs. 30–35 *{{Endn|2}}: [http://www.games-workshop.com/gws/catalog/productDetail.jsp?catId=&prodId=prod1700019a Games Workshop] *{{Endn|3}}: [[Dark Vengeance (Novella)]], pgs. 80–126 *{{Endn|4}}: [[Crimson Slaughter - A Codex: Chaos Space Marines Supplement]], {{Cite This}} *{{Endn|5}}: [[Black Crusade: Traitor's Hate]], Chapter 1 *{{Endn|6}}: [[Gathering Storm: Fall of Cadia]], Chapter 2 {{DEFAULTSORT:Kranon, Sevastus}} [[Category:Characters (Black Crusades)]] [[Category:Characters (Crimson Slaughter)]] [[Category:Characters (Khorne)]]

("Father" via [[Gene-Seed]]) |Occupation ='' '' *Member of the [[Luna Wolves]]/[[Sons of Horus]] (Former) *Member of the [[Crusader Host]] (Former) *Member of the [[Knights-Errant]] (Former) *One of the founding [[Grey Knights Grand Master|Grand Master]]s of the [[Grey Knights]]s |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Imperium of Man]] **[[Luna Wolves]] **[[Crusader Host]] **[[Knights-Errant]] **[[Grey Knights]] |Notes = }} '''Severian''' was a [[Luna Wolf]] and latent [[psyker]] during the [[Great Crusade]] and [[Horus Heresy]]. He would later be recruited by [[Malcador (Character)|Malcador the Sigillite]] into the [[Knights-Errant]].{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|2}} ===History=== ====The Great Crusade==== Severian served as one of the [[Crusader Host]] stationed on [[Terra]] at the onset of the [[Great Crusade]]. Severian served on Terra for one hundred and seventy years and was absent for the majority of the Great Crusade.{{Fn|1a}} {{Fn|2}} ====The Outcast Dead==== {{Spoiler|source=The Outcast Dead (Novel)}} Because of his genetic affiliations with a [[Traitor Legion]], Severian was imprisoned in the [[Khangba Marwu]] along with the other Crusader Host members from the Traitor Legions.{{fn|1c}} During his imprisonment, [[Magnus the Red]] sent his psychic warning to the [[Emperor]] about [[Horus]]'s imminent rebellion.{{fn|1b}} Severian and his fellows were freed by [[Atharva]] of the [[Thousand Sons]]. Severian and Atharva were able to lead the Outcast Dead effortlessly out of Khangba Marwa, an action thought impossible.{{fn|1d}} Atharva's plan was to capture the [[Astropath]] [[Kai Zulane]] and present him to the Emperor, to validate Magnus's warning of Horus's betrayal, before anybody else were to retrieve that knowledge from [[Kai Zulane]]'s mind, as it was for the Emperor's eyes only. The other Space Marines thought Atharva only needed him because of his abilities for their flight home. The Outcast Dead would eventually be tracked down to the Temple of Woe in the Petitioner's City, where they made their last stand against the Imperial forces pursuing them.{{fn|1f}} The majority of the Outcast Dead died fighting{{fn|1g}}{{fn|1h}} and Atharva was executed as a traitor by [[Rogal Dorn]]{{fn|1i}}, but Severian used his role as a scout to make his escape.{{Fn|1e}} ====The Wolf Hunt==== Two days later Rogal Dorn would task the expert hunter, [[Nagasena]], a descendant of the last Samurai of Terra, with the death of Severian. Nagasena easily tracked the warrior through the streets of the Petitioner's City, even going so far as to communicate with him via the vox-network in the scavenged helmet that Severian wore. Nagasena noted that Severian identified himself as a Luna Wolf, not a Son of Horus, and was infuriated at the accusations leveled against his [[Primarch]]. Curious as to where Severian's loyalties truly lay, Nagasena let Severian live despite having him in the sights of his [[Long-Las]] rifle. Severian stole into the private estate of [[Vadok Singh]], the Emperor's personal architect. He intended to take the warmason hostage and use an orbit capable shuttle to return to his Legion with either a warning of the lies being spread of Terra, or to call Horus to account for his treachery. Nagasena met Severian in single combat and was easily beaten by the Luna Wolf, who knocked Singh out and carried him to the landing pads. Nagasena used his [[volkite]] pistol to disable the shuttle, causing it to crash. Nagasena offered Severian one last chance to be taken alive, and he refused. Though his pistol was master-crafted, the shot meant to kill Severian shorted out and before Nagasena could fix the gun, [[Malcador]]'s agents arrived. The [[Sigillite]] revealed that he was blocking the built-up energies of the pistol with his mind and bade Nagasena to deactivate the weapon. Malcador had Severian taken into custody, stating that the unique precognitive gifts of the loyal Luna Wolf would be put to use in the newly formed [[Grey Knights]]. Finally, Malcador told Nagasena that he too would have a new place, as a tracker and hunter in the newly formed [[Inquisition]]{{Fn|2}} ====Molech==== Later, Severian was part of a team of [[Knights-Errant]] led by [[Garviel Loken]] to attempt to infiltrate and mark the [[Vengeful Spirit]]. After a fierce fight their mission failed, but Severian was able to escape with Loken.{{Fn|3}} ====Iapto==== Severian later appeared among the nine chosen by Malcador to become the founding members of the [[Grey Knight]]s. He was reunited with Garviel Loken one last time before assuming the mantle '''Iapto''', who would become one of the original [[Grey Knights Grand Master]]s.{{Fn|4}} At an unknown time later, Severian was slain. [[Abaddon the Despoiler]] personally witnessing his death.{{Fn|5}} ===Trivia=== {{Trivia}} *Iapto is an alternate spelling for [[Wikipedia:Iapetus|Iapetus]], one of the original Greek Titans and the son of Gaia and Uranus. ===Sources=== *{{Endn|1}}: [[The Outcast Dead (Novel)]], {{Cite This}} **{{endn|1a}}: ''Dramatis Personae'' **{{endn|1b}}: ch. 7 **{{endn|1c}}: ch. 13 **{{endn|1d}}: ch. 14 **{{endn|1e}}: ch. 21 **{{endn|1f}}: ch. 22 **{{endn|1g}}: ch. 23 **{{endn|1h}}: ch. 24 **{{endn|1i}}: ch. 25 *{{Endn|2}}: [[Wolf Hunt (Audio Book)]], {{Cite This}} *{{Endn|3}}: [[Vengeful Spirit (Novel)]], {{Cite This}} *{{Endn|4}}: [[The Buried Dagger (Novel)]], Chapter 7 *{{Endn|5}}: [[Pandorax (Novel)]] - Chapter 18, 157961.M41 / The Underhive. Severina Raine.wikitext:
{{Character |Portal ={{AstraMilitarumPortal}} |Name ={{PAGENAME}} |Image =HBArt.jpg |Caption = |Title = |Homeworld =[[Darpex]]{{Fn|2a}} |Birth =c. 900s.[[M41]]{{Fn|2a}} |Active Period =c. 900s.[[M41]] - Present |Death = |Cause of Death = |Species =[[Human]] |Type = |Gender =Female |Relatives =[[Lucia Raine]]
(Sister){{Fn|2c}} |Occupation =[[Commissar]] of the [[Imperial Guard]] |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Imperium of Man]] **[[Imperial Guard]] ***[[11th Antari Rifles]] |Notes = }} '''Severina Raine''' is a [[Commissar]] who is attached to the [[11th Antari Rifles]]{{Fn|1}}. ===History=== For years, Severina was haunted by the idea that her sister and fellow Commissar [[Lucia Raine]] was a traitor to the [[Imperium]]. The shame drove her to become even more rigid and uncompromising.{{Fn|2c}} However she later discovered that Lucia had found out about a conspiracy within the [[Bale Stars Crusade]] involving the corrupt [[Lord Militant]] [[Alar Serek]] and was eliminated and framed to silence her.{{Fn|2f}} The 11th Antari Rifles are currently among the Imperial forces fighting in a campaign to save the Imperial worlds of the Bale Stars from an invasion by the [[Sighted]] [[Chaos Cult]]{{Fn|2}}. During the effort to save the world [[Drast]], she fought beside the [[Astra Militarum Company|Company]] of [[Imperial Guard Captain|Captain]] [[Tevar Lun]] and was forced to execute him, after he refused what he claimed was a suicidal order to storm an enemy held fortress. Raine knew her execution of the well respected Captain, risked earning the angry resentment of the Company, but she reminded Lun's Company that their orders came from the campaign's commander, [[Lord General Militant]] [[Alar Serek]] and above all the [[Emperor]] himself.{{Fn|1}} She then took command of the Company and told them as a Commissar, she represented the will of the Emperor and to refuse her orders is to refuse him as well. This caused the [[Guardsmen]]'s anger to dissipate, though Raine knew some still held a grudge against her. That mattered little to her though and with the Company willingly under her command, they stormed the fortress. While they suffered heavy losses, the Company succeeded in planting explosives within the fortress and then escaped before it exploded.{{Fn|1}} ====Laxus Secundus==== Alongside the Antari Rifles, Raine fought to secure the [[Forge World]] of [[Laxus Secundus]] from a [[Chaos Cult]] known as [[The Sighted]] during the [[Bale Stars Crusade]]. Facing stiff resistance, including from [[Traitor Guard]] [[Baneblade]]s and corrupted [[Battle-Automata]], they battled towards the heavy fortified Delta Gate.{{Fn|2a}} The situation seemed hopeless for the Imperials until the arrival of [[Lord Militant]] [[Alar Serek]] and reinforcements.{{Fn|2a}} After capturing Laxus' primary Forge, Raine and the Antari Rifles were reassigned by [[Lord Commissar]] [[Mardan Tula]] to support the forces of the rival Commissar [[Lukas Vander]]. During her investigations into how enemy forces were able to obtain advanced equipment, Raine discovered deep corruption in high command which implicated [[General]] [[Kaspar Sylar]] of the [[Kavrone Dragoons]], who she suspected may have had a hand in the illness which claimed Lord Militant Serek shortly after his arrival.{{Fn|2b}}{{Fn|2c}} Despite this, Raine was unable to come across any clear conclusive evidence, and was forced to lead an assault on the enemy fortress known as the Sanctum of Bones in the hopes of killing the Sighted leader, the [[Rogue Psyker|Witch]] [[Cretia Ommatid]].{{Fn|2d}} During the battle, the Imperial [[Tempestus Scion]] squad known as the [[Duskhounds]] led by Captain [[Andren Fel]] infiltrate the fortress to disable its [[Void Shield]]s. During the infiltration, they learned that the Cultists were receiving aid by a figure known as "The Manticore" before driving off Cretia Ommatid. Fel later learned that Lord Militant had in fact survived, and was covering up his own death.{{Fn|2e}} As the Imperials fought inside the Sanctum of Bone, Raine and Vander were separated from their forces and forced into a tenuous alliance to survive. Eventually rendezvousing with the Imperials, Raine finds out that Fel has since been the target of a bomb plot due to his knowledge of Serek, and that there was a conspiracy in High Command to "achieve immortality".{{Fn|2f}} Shortly after, Serek reemerges to order the Antari on a suicide mission to silence them. Raine public ally accused Serek of treason and is forced to flee, but not before faking her own death at the Laxian Shipyards.{{Fn|2g}} As the Imperials began their assault on the Laxian Shipyards, the Antari Rifles suffered devastating losses. [[Sergeant]] [[Daven Wyck]] was able to make it to the enemy encampment and set off explosives, but was critically wounded and saved by the [[Sanctioned Psyker]] [[Lydia Zane]].{{Fn|2h}} Nonetheless, thanks to their sacrifice the Imperials were able to capture the shipyards, and at the subsequent victory ceremony Raine reemerged, alive. She exposed Serek as the "Manticore", revealing his use of [[Sorcery]] to cheat his earlier death. In the ensuing firefight, Vander killed Sylar while Raine executed Serek. In the aftermath of the debacle, High Command covered up Serek and Sylar's treason to maintain morale. Severus XIII.wikitext:
[[Image:Severus13.jpg|thumb|right|Severus XIII{{Fn|1}}]]
'''Severus XIII''' is the current ruling member of House Severus, a once-powerful aristocratic house in the [[Calixis Sector]]. Continuing the tradition began by his ancestor [[Severus I]] in [[M39]], Severus XIII maintains a bitterness against the [[Imperium]] for denying his family control over the [[Periphery Sub-Sector]] and lusts for power. He would go on to covertly use the [[Dark Eldar]] [[Kabal]] known as the [[Children of Thorns]] to gain control of much of the Sub-Sector, ruling it as his private fiefdom. However after the invasion by the [[Ork]] [[Warboss]] [[Ghenghiz Grimtoof]], his Dark Eldar allies abandoned him and Severus was forced to plea to the Imperium for aid. What began was a collection of campaigns known as the [[Spinward Front]], which dramatically escalated when Severus XIII annexed the worlds he ruled as his personal fiefdom known as the [[Severan Dominate]]. Since then, Severus XIII has been declared to be a traitor to the Imperium by Sector authorities.{{Fn|1}}

Seydon.wikitext:
{{SpaceMarinesPortal}}

'''Seydon''' is the eighteenth [[Chapter Master|Master]] of the [[Iron Snakes]] [[Space Marine Chapter]]. A gigantic figure standing a metre than the average [[battle-brother]], Seydon is noted for his wisdom and leadership, knowing the names and qualities of many, if not all of the thousand strong Astartes who serve under him. Despite being the eighteenth Chapter Master, Seydon is old enough to remember the original Sergeant Damocles of [[Damocles Squad]] and was the one who told him to form the squad.{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|1e}}{{Fn|2}}

He personally led twenty five squads in the defence of [[Ganahedarak]] against an [[Ork|Orkish]] incursion and made excellent initial headway. With the patience of one who had reduced worlds to cinders in they're time, he ignored the beasts taunts and had them attack his fortified position instead of taking the fight to them, throwing back each assault and inflicting massive casualties. However, the arrival of a second horde swung the balance of the battle in the Greenskins favour and forced Seydon to pull back his forces to a series of round houses constructed for the Iron Snakes by local rulers. Cut off and massively outnumbered, Seydon's force would have been annihilated if not for the internecine conflict that plagued the Greenskins and a relief force of a further five squads lead by [[Librarian]] [[Petrok]] who cut their way through to Seydon and successfully broke them out of the Greenskin encirclement. Exhausted from battle and greatly shaken by chapter's failure to fulfill their oaths of protection to the people of Ganahedarak and by the loss of sixty one battle brothers, including the entirety of [[First Company|Notable]] Squad Parthus, he still retained the wits to agree to a plan proposed by Petrok and [[Brother-Sergeant]] [[Priad]] that lead the Ork hordes away from the [[Reef Stars]] and back to the [[Dark Eldar]] who had first guided them there.{{Fn|1b}}{{Fn|1c}}{{Fn|1d}}{{Fn|1e}}

==Appearance==
Gigantic, robed and mysterious, Seydon wears a cloak made of broken, polished wyrm-horn pieces linked together like a jigsaw puzzle by gold wire which covers the exchanger tanks he uses to breathe. In battle he bears the great lance, '''Tiborus'''.{{Fn|1b}}{{Fn|1e}}

'''Sha'vastos''' is a [[T'au Commander]] and skilled T'au [[Battlesuit]] pilot and a member of [[The Eight]], [[Farsight]]'s elite honour guard.{{Fn|1}}

===History===
The first [[T'au]] to be fitted with a [[Puretide Neurochip]], Sha'vastos faced lobotomy when the [[Ethereal Council]] ordered the removal of all Puretide Neurochips after they had been found wanting. {{PAGENAME}} was saved this fate by the intervention of Commander Farsight.{{Fn|2}} By the [[Arkunasha War]] the elderly Fire Warrior was one of the finest T'au soldiers Farsight knew, and joined his growing corps of officers.{{Fn|2}} His prototype neurochip suffered rapid degeneration after the battle, however, so Farsight had him spirited away in a stasis pod until he could find a cure. Many decades later, [[O'Vesa]] was able to recalibrate the neurochip and reawaken the old warrior.{{Fn|1}} Despite Shavatos's returning function, at times, especially while under stress, the Puretide engram would reassert control. In these moments, Farsight could converse with his old master{{Fn|2}}, or even allow Puretide to bring his considerable command skills to bear.{{Fn|3b}} On occasions Sha'vastos could stop the engram from taking control, though it required immense effort.{{Fn|3a}}

===Wargear===
Sha'vastos goes into battle in a modified [[XV8 Crisis Battlesuit]] equipped with a [[Plasma Rifle]], [[Tau Flamer]], [[Shield Generator]], two [[Gun Drone]]s, and vectored retro-thursters. The suit is directed by his Puretide Engram chip.{{Fn|1}}

Shai Arrian.wikitext:
{{AstraMilitarumPortal}}
'''Shai Arrian''' was a [[Cadian Shock Troopers|Cadian]] [[Astra Militarum]] [[Marshal (Imperial Guard)|Marshal]] who defended the [[Fortress World]], during the [[13th Black Crusade]].

However after [[Cadia]] suffered a death blow at hands of [[Abaddon the Despoiler]], Arrian was able to escape aboard the [[Claymore Class Corvette]] ''[[Lord-Lieutenant Berwicke]]'' with [[General]] [[Gruber]], before the Fortress World was destroyed. When the Imperials later escaped from the [[Cadian System]] though, a [[Warp]] mishap separated the ''Berwicke'' and three other ships from the rest of the Imperial warships. They later found themselves in the [[Chaos]]-invaded [[Agripinaa System]]{{Fn|1a}} and soon came under attack from the warships of the [[Sons of Malice]].{{Fn|1b}} Only the ''Berwicke'' and the ''[[Venerable Warrior]]'' were able to escape, but the Sons of Malice pursued them and General Gruber knew they would not be able to outrun the Warband. As he was the ranking officer, Gruber ordered the ''Berwicke'' and ''Venerable Warrior'' to deploy the Cadians on [[Morten's Quay]]'s ice mining moon, [[Faith's Anchorage]] and then do all they could to reach Terra and report Cadia's fate.{{Fn|1c}} However, the ships were destroyed by the Sons of Malice before they could escape the System and the Warband then invaded Faith's Anchorage.{{Fn|1d}} In the [[Battle of Faith's Anchorage|battle that followed]], Arrian and the Cadians under General Gruber's command were overwhelmed by the Warband's sheer numbers and were mercilessly killed.{{Fn|1e}}

'''Shalaxi Helbane''', known as the '''Monarch of the Hunt'''{{Fn|3a}}, is a [[Slaanesh]]i [[Keeper of Secrets]] and is the undisputed martial champion amongst the [[Chaos God]]'s [[Daemon]]s.{{Fn|1}}

===Overview===
Shalaxi was created by Slaanesh to fight and defeat rival [[Greater Daemons]], especially [[Khorne]]'s [[Bloodthirsters]], and Shalaxi has bested some of the most formidable adversaries in the galaxy. If rumours are to be believed, this includes the dreaded Bloodthirster [[Skarbrand]] himself.{{Fn|1}} Myths also tell of Helbane's quest into the [[Garden of Nurgle]] to bring the [[Prince of Corpseblooms]] to the [[Palace of Slaanesh]].{{Fn|5}} Besides immaterial foes, past targets of Shalaxi have included regents, warlords, [[Tyranid]] monstrosities, [[Knight]]s, and [[C'tan Shard]]s.{{Fn|6}}

Shalaxi tracks and pursues the greatest prey no matter where in existence they attempt to hide. Able to track their quarry across any environment, space, or dimension, sooner of later they will invariably run their foe to ground and engage them in battle. The more powerful the prey, the greater the torment Shalaxi will inflict upon them.{{Fn|6}}

===History===
Some six hundred years before the formation of the [[Great Rift]], Shalaxi Helbane was banished to the [[Warp]] by the [[Grey Knights]]. Angered, Slaanesh imprisoned Helbane in the Palace of Punishments. However, Slaanesh eventually judged that Shalaxi had atoned for its failure, and dispatched the Daemon to halt the rise of [[Ynnead]] and foil the plans of the [[Ynnari]]. The Daemon was able to travel to [[Belial IV]] and steal the fifth [[Crone Sword]], placing it far from the reach of the Ynnari in the [[Palace of Slaanesh]].{{Fn|3a}}

Helbane gathered many old allies to its cause - amongst them [[Syll'Esske]] and a warband of [[Herald of Slaanesh|Slaaneshi Heralds]]. Entering the Webway, Helbane was able to use its synesthetic ability to track [[Yvraine]]'s soul-trail. Helbane tracked down the Ynnari leader to [[Threccia]]. However, Yvraine was [[Battle of Threccia|able to escape]] as Shalaxi raged.{{Fn|3a}} Shalaxi was later again able to corner Yvraine on the world of [[Iathglas]]. During the [[Battle of Iathglas|subsequent battle]], the creature managed to hold off the combined forces of Yvraine, the [[Yncarne]], [[The Visarch|the Visarch]], [[Jain Zar]], [[Lelith Hesperax]], and a [[Solitaire]]. Shalaxi was apparently defeated, but revealed that it had only been an illusion solid enough to give good sport and little else. Helbane gloated that Slaanesh considered the Ynnari little more than playthings as its glamour vanished, pledging to one day slay Yvraine.{{Fn|3b}}

===Wargear===
Shalaxi goes into battle wielding a '''living whip''' and the [[Daemon Weapon|daemon spear]] [[Soulpiercer]], wearing a '''shining aegis''', and arraigned in the [[Cloak of Constriction]].{{fn|5}}

("Brothers" via [[gene-seed]]) |Occupation ='' '' *[[Lord Commander]] of the [[Night Lords]] *[[Equerry]] to [[Konrad Curze]] |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Imperium of Man]] (Former) **[[Night Lords]] *[[Carrion Realms]] |Notes = }} '''Shang''' (sometimes spelled as '''Sheng'''{{Fn|1}}) was a [[Lord Commander]]{{Fn|3}} of the [[Night Lords]] during the [[Great Crusade]] and [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|1}} ===History=== Serving as the [[Equerry]] of [[Primarch]] [[Konrad Curze]], Shang was a close Confidant and aid of the Night Haunter. Unlike [[Sevatar]] he was genuinely loyal to Curze as opposed to his mission to rule through fear. Curze considered Shang one of his few sons that he did not hate, which is why he made him his equerry. However Curze did see Shang's devotion as a weakness that could be manipulated. During the destruction of [[Nostramo]], Shang pleaded with Sevatar to try and halt Curze's rampage. Sevatar refused and condemned Shang as weak, but the Equerry in turn was the first Night Lord to point out that Curze was going mad.{{Fn|3}} During the [[Thramas Crusade]] Shang accompanied his Primarch and [[Sevatar]] to the surface of [[Tsagualsa]] in the meeting with [[Dark Angels]] Primarch [[Lion El'Jonson]] and his own [[Honour Guard]]. In the subsequent fight between the two sides, Shang helped return the wounded Curze to safety after he helped kill the Dark Angels Captain [[Alajos]].{{Fn|1}} After the disappearance of Curze, Shang became emotionally broken but was determined to reforge the Legion and find their missing Primarch. However he became embroiled in a vicious power struggle with [[Gendor Skraivok]]. Shang maintained that the future of the Legion lay with reaving and finding Curze, while Skraivok wanted to rejoin [[Horus]] and push on [[Terra]]. Ultimately Shang attempted to dispose of Skraivok by locking him in the maze aboard the ''[[Nightfall]]''. However thanks to his [[Daemon Weapon]] Skraivok was able to escape and easily slew Shang in a duel, gaining the supremacy of the Night Lords in the process.{{Fn|2}} ===Sources=== *{{Endn|1}}: [[Savage Weapons (Short Story)]] *{{Endn|2}}: [[The Painted Count (Short Story)]] *{{Endn|3}}: [[Konrad Curze: The Night Haunter (Novel)]] Chapter 11-12 [[Category:Characters (Night Lords)]] [[Category:Characters (Deceased)]] [[fr:Sheng]]

'''Shas'O Dal'yth Ko'vash Kha'drel''', better known as '''Commander Bravestorm''', is a [[T'au Commander]].{{Fn|4a}}

===Biography===
Bravestorm was a faithful servant of the [[T'au Empire]] who helped repel the [[Imperial]] [[Operation Pluto|invasion]] of [[Dal'yth]] during the [[Damocles Crusade|Imperial advance into the Empire's territory]].{{Fn|4a}}

One of the original recipients of the experimental [[Battlesuit]] weapon known as the [[Onager Gauntlet]], during the [[Damocles Crusade]]{{Fn|4x}} Bravestorm's Battlesuit was critically damaged at [[Blackthunder Mesa]] after he took down dozens of Imperial vehicles{{Fn|1}} as well as a [[Titan]].{{Fn|6}} Now entombed in life support systems, he became confined to his Battlesuit and went on to serve the during the [[Farsight Expedition]]. During the campaign Bravestorm was a major T'au Commander who slew scores of Orks despite taking grievous injuries to his already damaged form.{{Fn|3}} During the war on [[Vior'los]] against [[Hive Fleet Gorgon]], he sacrificed himself by ramming his battlesuit into a [[Bio-Titan]]{{Fn|8a}} but was again able to be salvaged.{{Fn|8b}} Bravestorm continues to serve the [[Farsight Enclaves]] as part of [[The Eight]].{{Fn|2}}

During the fighting on [[Arthas Moloch]] in the [[Arks of Omen Campaign]], Bravestorm's [[Iridium]] Battlesuit suffered catastrophic damage from [[Ork]] fire. Farsight personally oversaw his evacuation to a medical facility.{{Fn|7}}

===Wargear===
While still a member of the [[T'au Empire]] proper, Bravestorm piloted an experimental prototype [[Crisis Battlesuit#XV8-02 Crisis 'Iridium' Battlesuit|XV8-02 Battlesuit]], equipped with a [[plasma rifle]], a [[Tau Flamer]], a [[shield generator]], and [[Gun Drone]] [[Oe-ven-3]].{{Fn|4a}}

===Trivia===
{{Trivia}}
*By the [[T'au Naming Conventions]], it can be surmised that Bravestorm is from [[Dal'yth]] [[Sept]].

===Conflicting sources===
*During the [[Second Agrellan Campaign]], Bravestorm sacrificed himself to save [[Farsight]] from a [[Vindicare Assassin]]'s bullet.{{Fn|3}} This is not mentioned in more recent lore about the character, such as in [[Psychic Awakening: The Greater Good]].{{Fn|5}}

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was a [[Tau Commander]] in charge of [[T'au]] forces on [[Kronus]].

==History==
In 740.M41, Shas'O Kais was dispatched with the [[Fire Caste]] alongside [[Tau Auxiliaries]] forces including the [[Vespid]] and [[Kroot]], to quell the troubles on [[Kronus]]. He was also dispatched with the [[Ethereal]] Aun'el [[Shi'Ores]] to secure and hold the capital city on Kronus. The planet was caught in a battle between the [[Imperium of Mankind]]'s [[Imperial Guard]] and [[Blood Ravens]] [[Chapter]] of [[Astartes]], the [[Eldar]], and the [[Necrons]]. A strong yet merciful commander, O'Kais often offered his enemies multiple chances to surrender, with refusal to serve the greater good resulting in the enemy's total annihilation.{{Fn|1}} However, the [[Blood Ravens]] managed to drive the Tau forces off the world during the campaign.{{Fn|2}}

==Wargear==
Kais wears experimental [[XV22 Stealth Battlesuit]] armour, a symilar type as [[Commander Shadowsun]], which throughout the campaign gains a [[Jetpack]], Advanced Sensor Array and [[Stealth field generator]]. Initially armed with only a [[Burst Cannon]], Kais has access to a plethora of ranged weapon upgrades including [[Missile Pod]]s, a [[Fusion Blaster]] and a [[Plasma Rifle]]. He can also be accompanied by various [[Drone|Shield drones]] and [[Drone|Gun drones]].{{Fn|1}}

==Trivia==
{{Trivia}}
*There are three prominent Tau Fire Caste members named Kais. In 2001 the video game [[Warhammer 40,000: Fire Warrior]] released, alongside a companion novel, with the main character named [[Shas'la T'au Kais]]. When [[Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War - Dark Crusade]] was released in 2006 there was much speculation that the leader of Tau forces in the game, who this article is about, was the same Kais after having been elevated to [[T%27au_Lexicon#Caste_System|'O]] rank. Relic entertainment employees gave contradictory answers. Later appearances of a [[Shas'O Monat Kais|Shas'O Kais]] in Tau codices and [[Phil Kelly]] novels have also been speculated by fans to be the same Kais. Phil Kelly has been vauge about who the Kais in his novels is. Chronologically speaking, it is unlikely Shas'la T'au Kais is the Shas'O Kais from Dawn of War, as the events of Dawn of War happen before the events of Fire Warrior.

(Father) |Occupation ='' *[[Fire Warrior]] **[[Shas'la]] (former) **[[Shas'ui]] |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' *[[Tau Empire]] **[[T'au (Planet)|T'au]] |Notes = }} '''Shas'ui T'au Kais'''{{Fn|1}} was a [[Tau]] [[Fire Warrior]] who played a major role in the rescue attempt of the kidnapped [[Ethereal]] El'Ko'vash. ===Overview=== Late in the [[M41|41st Millennium]], the Ethereal [[Aun'el Ko'vash]] was kidnapped by [[Space Marines]] of the [[Raptors]] chapter under the orders of Imperial Governor Severus. The [[Tau]] response was swift. [[Fire Warrior]]s descended upon the world of [[Dolumar IV]] with a vengeance, intent on getting their Ethereal back. One of these Fire Warriors was a young [[Shas'la]] by the name of Kais. In his very first battle, his [[Trial by Fire]], Kais proved instrumental not only in the initial rescue, but also in the resulting battle against the forces of [[Chaos]], who had orchestrated the entire incident in an attempt to release the [[Daemon]] [[Tarkh'ax]] from a dimensional prison. Guided only by his commander Shas'el T'au Lusha, and later [[Captain]] [[Ardias]], Commander of the 3rd Company of the [[Ultramarines]], Kais fought through a hell of blood and fire before finally facing down Tarkh'ax himself. Reports on the incident are varied, and often contradictory. Some claim that Kais was able to defeat the [[Daemon]] singlehandedly, while others state that he was helped by both Captain Ardias and a [[Battlesuit#XV81_Crisis_Battlesuit|Crisis Suit]] team led by [[El'Lusha]]. In the end, Ko'vash was unfortunately killed, and Dolumar IV was duly cleansed by the [[Imperial Navy]]. Kais ended up in a mental hospital suffering from a extremely severe case of post-traumatic stress disorder. It is possible that he may recover himself of the Mont'au within, perhaps using the sliver of display wafer given by his father as a guide. The display wafer given to him by his father reads: {{QuoteBox |quote= ''My son,''
''No expansion without equilibrium.''
''No conquest without control.''
''Pursue success in serenity''
''And service to the [[tau'va]].''
''With pride.''
''Shas'o T'au Shi'ur'' }} The remaining sliver only reads "With pride." Kais doesn't need the rest because he had memorized it. He crushed the wafer on Dolumar IV and the only reason he has this sliver is because El'Lusha found it while tracking Kais and put it in his hand at the hospital. ===Trivia=== {{Trivia}} *There are three prominent Tau Fire Caste members named Kais.
