([[Ta'lissera|Bond-mate]]) |Occupation =[[Tau Commander|Supreme Commander]] of the [[Tau Empire]] |Preceded by =[[O'Shovah]] (As Supreme Commander) |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Tau Empire]] **[[Vior'la]] |Notes = }} ''' Shas’O Vior’la Shas’len’ra M’yen Sha’serra ''', also known as '''Commander Shadowsun''',{{Fn|13b}} is the current [[Tau Empire]] supreme [[Tau Commander|commander]]. ===Biography=== ====Tutelage Under Puretide==== The young Shas spent much of her youth on [[Dal'yth]] as a student of the famed [[Commander Puretide]] alongside his other pupils [[Commander Farsight|Shoh]] and [[Kais]]. Together, they braved the harsh and frigid conditions of Mount Kan'ji. All three survived and were accepted as full students of Puretide. Shas would go on to become a famous subordinate of Shoh, who became known as [[Commander Farsight]].{{Fn|13c}} ====Early Career==== Years later, O'Shaserra was selected to replace the now-rogue Farsight during the [[Damocles Crusade]] and [[K'resh Expansion]] during the [[Great War of Confederation]].{{Fn|3}} It was on [[K'resh]] that O'Shaserra acquired her nickname - Shadowsun - as she used an eclipse to ambush and destroy a vast Ork horde.{{Fn|5}} Shadowsun seems to be a more steadfast leader, more suited to the job of overseeing the [[Third Sphere of Expansion]]. It was [[Aun'Va]] who selected Shadowsun, in hopes of replicating the strategic brilliance of Puretide. Aun'va recognized that disciples of the aging Puretide were indispensable, and Shadowsun was among those students put into [[Cryostasis Unit|cryogenic stasis]] for future expansion campaigns that would occur beyond the natural lifespan of the Tau. Shadowsun was unfrozen during the [[Great War of Confederation]], and was instrumental in the Tau victory over the [[Orks]].{{Fn|3}} When she learned of the betrayal of Commander Farsight, she went into the training dome of the '''Mont'yr''' and destroyed the last statue of Farsight with the twin [[Fusion Blaster]]s of her [[XV22 Stealth Battlesuit]], swearing to spread the [[Greater Good]] with pride and honour. Shadowsun became known as the master of the [[Kauyon]] tactics.{{Fn|5}} She also led several raids against a [[Tyranid]] splinter fleet and managed to do so much damage to the hive ships that the Tau fleet was able to fully engage the Tyranid fleet, without losing any ships.{{cite this}} ====Third Sphere of Expansion==== Under her leadership, the T'au Empire has again grown with the [[Third Sphere of Expansion]], formimg five colonies in a halo around the original [[Sept]] worlds, including in the [[Damocles Gulf]], [[Perdus Rift]] and much further afield. This success was due in part to the Imperium being distracted elsewhere and the Tyranids and Orks being temporarily contained. Shadowsun went on to score a decisive victory over the [[Imperium]] in the [[Battle for Mu'gulath Bay]], one of the greatest Tau victories over the Imperium.{{Fn|1}} [[Image:ShadowsunNov.jpg|thumb|right|220px|O'Shaserra{{Fn|2}}]] However it was at Mu'gulath Bay that Shadowsun encountered [[Kor'sarro Khan]] of the [[White Scars]], who inflicted horrendous casualties upon her command staff and drove the normally calm Tau Commander into a fury. In her rage and overconfidence, Shadowsun led an offensive that resulted in a stinging Tau [[Battle of Voltoris|defeat]]. Having barely escaped the Imperial ambush with her life, which was only thanks to the brave sacrifice of her personal retinue, Shadowsun swore to redouble her efforts in the [[Third Sphere of Expansion]]. This led to her initiating the [[Prefectia Campaign]].{{Fn|3}} Though successful at Prefectia, Shadowsun was surprised when the Imperium used the war as a distraction to strike at Mu'gulath Bay once more. During the [[Second Agrellan Campaign|second battle]] for the world, Shadowsun led an effective resistance but could not stop the destruction of Mu'gulath Bay or the death of [[Aun'va]] at the hands of the [[Officio Assassinorum]]. Shadowsun herself only survived the destruction of Mu'gulath Bay due to her earlier wounding at the hands of a [[Callidus Assassin]], which forced her to recover aboard a Tau starship. Free from the restraint of Aun'va and grateful to [[O'Shovah]] for aid during the battle, Shadowsun secretly leaked information to her former ally that the [[Ethereal Council]] had ordered her to capture him.{{Fn|4}} ====Fifth Sphere of Expansion==== Later, Shadowsun was taken out of cryo-stasis to command the newly christened [[Fifth Sphere of Expansion]] on the other side of the [[Startide Nexus]]. During the fighting, Shadowsun expressed frustration with [[Fourth Sphere of Expansion|Fourth Sphere]] Tau led by [[Surestrike]], which displayed excessive brutality and xenophobia. Shadowsun, with the cooperation of the [[Ethereal Council]], eventually disciplined the Fourth Sphere commanders.{{Fn|6a}} Shortly after she engaged in [[Battle of the Startide Nexus|overseeing the defense]] of the [[Startide Nexus]] against [[Death Guard]] forces.{{Fn|6b}} During the campaign in the Startide Nexus, Shadowsun attempted to learn the truth of the [[4th Sphere of Expansion]] and the mysterious [[Warp Entity]] they encountered within the [[Warp]]. For these actions she was briefly relieved of command by the [[Ethereal]] [[Aun'la]] and replaced with [[Commander Surestrike]].{{Fn|13d}} However Shadowsun gathered a small group of [[Tau Auxiliaries]] which included the [[Kroot]] [[Opikh Tak]], [[Nicassar]] [[Ven Tah Regah]], and [[Charpactin]] [[A'haia]] and boarded the Death Guard Battleship ''Nephylum''. During the subsequent battle Shadowsun was sucked into the void of space but seemingly saved by the same Tau [[Goddess T'au'va|Warp entity that had delivered the 4th Sphere of Expansion]]. Afterwards, she was reestablished by Aun'la as Supreme Commander.{{Fn|13e}} After the mysterious conclusion of the battle, Shadowsun directed Fifth Sphere campagins at the [[Chalnath Expanse]] and [[Razing of Astorgius|Astorgius]].{{Fn|10}} She is currently organizing a defense of the Fifth Sphere against a massive [[Ork]] horde threatening the [[Chalnath Expanse]] and the [[Nem'yar Atoll]].{{Fn|12a}} ===Weargear=== Commander Shadowsun originally wore an [[XV22 Stealth Battlesuit]] into battle incorporating both a stealth generator and a jump pack. She was accompanied by a [[Drone#Command-link Drones|Command-link Drone]] and two [[MV52 Shield Drone]]s and was armed with dual Fusion Blasters which enable her to take on enemy heavy armour, she also carried a [[Bonding Knife]].{{Fn|11}} Since the formation of the [[Great Rift]], Shadowsun has been issued an upgraded XV22 Stalker Battlesuit equipped with twin [[Fusion Blaster|High-Energy Fusion Blaster]]s, Light [[Missile Pod]]{{Fn|12b}}, [[Flechette Discharger|Flechette Launcher]]{{Fn|12b}}, and is accompanied by an [[MV37 Advanced Guardian Drone]] designated ''Oe-hei''{{Fn|13a}} and a [[MV62 Command-Link Drone]] designated ''Oe-ken-yon''{{Fn|13a}}{{Fn|9}}. ===Images=== O'Shaserra3.jpg|Commander Shadowsun Shadowsun.gif|Commander Shadowsun miniature (4th Edition) Shadowsun8th.jpg|Shadowsun (8th Edition){{Fn|7}} JoytoyTauShadowsun.jpg|Shadowsun Joytoy figure{{Fn|14}} ===Sources=== {{Cite}} *{{Endn|1}}: [[Codex: Tau Empire (6th Edition)]], pg. 29 *{{Endn|2}}: [http://www.games-workshop.com/gws/wnt/blog.jsp?pid=8300054-gws Games Workshop Blog] *{{Endn|3}}: [[War Zone Damocles: Kauyon]], pgs. 6–7 *{{Endn|4}}: [[War Zone Damocles: Mont'ka]], pgs. 105–110 *{{Endn|5}}: [[Codex: Tau Empire (7th Edition)]], pg. 38 - {{Character |Portal ={{WhiteScarsPortal}} |Name ={{PAGENAME}} |Image =ShibanKhan.jpg |Caption ={{PAGENAME}}{{Fn|8}} |Title =Tachseer
Tamu (Former name) |Homeworld =[[Chogoris]] |Birth =c. [[M30]] |Active Period =[[M30]] - ??? |Death = |Cause of Death = |Species =[[Human]] |Type =[[Astartes]] |Gender =Male |Relatives =[[Jaghatai Khan]] ("Father" via [[gene-seed]]) |Occupation ='' '' *[[Space Marine Captain|Khan]] of the [[Brotherhood of the Storm]] *[[Master of the Hunt]] |Preceded by = |Succeeded by =[[Jubal Khan (Heresy)|Jubal Khan]] (As Master of the Hunt) |Faction ='' '' *[[Chogoris]] **[[Talskar]]s *[[Imperium of Man]] **[[White Scars]] |Notes = }} '''Shiban Khan''' was a member of the [[White Scars]] during the [[Great Crusade]] and early days of the [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|1b}} ===History=== Shiban was born '''Tamu''' in the Talskar region of [[Chogoris]], hailing from the '''Khin-zan''' Tribe. At 12 years old (8 in [[Terra]]n years) he was discovered after a local tribal battle by [[Targutai Yesugei]]. Upon initiation into the [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]], Tamu changed his name to Shiban and was inducted into the horde of [[Hasik Noyan-Khan]].{{Fn|1a}} Becoming the [[Khan]] of the Legion's [[Brotherhood of the Storm]]{{Fn|1b}}, Shiban was fiercely loyal to his [[Primarch]] [[Jaghatai Khan]]. During the Heresy while their Primarch was on [[Prospero]], Shiban discovered a plot by elements of the White Scars led by his friend and frequent brother-in-arms [[Torghun Khan]] and [[Hasik Noyan-Khan]] to take control of the Legion's fleet and ally with [[Warmaster]] [[Horus]].{{Fn|1c}} He led his Brotherhood aboard the ''[[Swordstorm]]'' to stop the conspirators from linking up with the [[Death Guard]], [[Second Battle of Prospero|buying enough time]] for Jaghatai to make it back to his ship.{{Fn|1d}}{{Fn|1e}}{{Fn|1f}} Four years after the events on [[Prospero]], much of Shiban's body was replaced by mechanical parts due to the vicious war of attrition, including his forearms, calves, thighs, and neck, which he dubbed the "Shackles." His men referred to him as "Tachseer" ("Restorer"), and he took many who were loyal from the rebellious brotherhoods under his own command. Shiban was changed over these years, becoming bitter, violent, and losing his signature laughter.{{Fn|2}} His reunion with [[Torghun Khan]] during the Scars rendezvous at [[Dark Glass]] went poorly when he condemned his former brother as a traitor and attempted to use him as cannon fodder against traitor forces. During the subsequent [[Battle of Catallus]], Shiban was defeated by the [[Emperor's Children]] [[Palatine Blades]] prefector [[Ravasch Cario]] but as the traitor was about to deliver the killing blow, he was overcome by his own [[Daemonic]] corruption. The moment gave Shiban the opening he needed to slay the Prefector.{{Fn|2a}} Later, Shiban took part in the [[Siege of Terra]] and was charged with the defenses of the [[Eternity Wall Spaceport]] alongside [[Imperial Fists]] Captain [[Camba-Diaz]], [[General|High Primary Solar General]] [[Saul Niborran]], and [[Sisters of Silence]] Commander [[Jenetia Krole]].{{Fn|3a}} During the battle, Shiban grew close to [[Imperial Army]] Captain [[Al-Nid Nazira]]. In the final stages of the battle, the Spaceport was overrun by the [[World Eaters]] and Shiban became determined to help evacuate some of his Imperial Army comrades. However as the shuttle took off, they were assailed by World Eaters. Though he had taken a vow to never take a step back and die in defense of the Port, Nazira risking his life to save him and the thought of using the shuttle's grav systems to kill many of the traitors spurred Shiban to turn around and make for the craft. Barely fighting off World Eaters to leap onto the flying shuttle, Shiban discovered that Nazira and the pilot were already slain by [[Bolter]] fire as the aircraft crashed into the Eternity Wall.{{Fn|3b}} Shiban survived the crash, but was horrifically wounded and stranded deep from Loyalist lines. Slowly making his way back to the Palace walls, he was plagued by visions of [[Targutai Yesugei]] and [[Torghun Khan]].{{Fn|4a}} Shiban eventually came upon a surviving [[Imperial Army]] Lieutenant [[Cole]], who was desperately trying to save an abandoned infant. Seeing this act as part of his fate, Shiban pledged to deliver Cole and the infant to the [[Inner Palace]]. Fighting through all kinds of Warp-spawned horrors with nothing but a broken metal pole, a badly injured Shiban managed to carrying the dying Cole as well as the infant back to the walls of the Palace.{{Fn|4d}} Now reunited with his legion, Shiban grimly continued the fight against the traitors while still yearning to speak to his old friend [[Torghun Khan]] one last time. He took part in Jaghatai Khan's massive attack to retake the [[Lion's Gate Spaceport]], taking part in the central thrust alongside the Primarch himself.{{Fn|5a}} Charged with taking the Spaceport's anti-ship orbital batteries, Shiban was not present when Jaghatai Khan disappeared following his victory over [[Mortarion]].{{Fn|5b}} Following the Khan's apparent death much of the White Scars initiated a death ritual to seemingly fight to their end. Alongside [[Ilya Ravallion]] Shiban was able to organize the surviving officers of the Legion and instead reinforce themselves at the Lion's Gate Spaceport once it was discovered the Primarch was still alive but badly wounded.{{Fn|5c}} As [[Sanguinius]] led the defence of the [[Eternity Gate (Imperial)|Eternity Gate]], Shiban and his White Scars worked to restore the defences of the Lion's Gate Spaceport. They eventually succeeded, unleashing a punishing anti-orbital bombardment upon the traitor armada that hung over Terra.{{Fn|6}} By this point, Shiban was declared the new [[Master of the Hunt]] by the White Scars and fought to defend the retaken Lion's Gate Spaceport.{{Fn|7}} Shiban survived the Siege, and after the battle had a reunion with [[Katsuhiro]] and the baby he had rescued. He arranged arrange for the two be flown from the ruins of the Palace to Katsuhiro's original home in the Dragon Nations.{{Fn|9}} Shortly after, he also bid goodbye to [[Ilya Ravallion]].{{Fn|9b}} ==Images== Image:ShibanArt.jpg|thumb|Shiban Khan during the [[Siege of Terra]]{{Fn|4d}} Image:ShibanPortrait.jpg|Shiban Khan as the Tachseer{{Fn|5}} ==Sources== *{{Endn|1}}: [[Scars (Novel)]] **{{Endn|1a}}: Prologue **{{Endn|1b}}: Chapter Twelve **{{Endn|1c}}: Chapter Seventeen **{{Endn|1d}}: Chapter Eighteen **{{Endn|1e}}: Chapter Twenty **{{Endn|1f}}: Chapter Twenty-Two *2: [[The Path of Heaven (Novel)]]: **{{Endn|2a}}: Chapters 21–25 *3: [[Saturnine (Novel)]]: **{{Endn|3a}}: Part 2, Chapter 5 **{{Endn|3b}} Part 3, Chapter 5 *4: [[Mortis (Novel)]]: **{{Endn|4a}}: Chapter 3 **{{Endn|4b}}: Chapter 10 **{{Endn|4c}}: Chapter 14 **{{Endn|4d}}: Chapter 22 *5: [[Warhawk (Novel)]]: **{{Endn|5a}}: Chapter 14 **{{Endn|5b}}: Chapter 20 **{{Endn|5c}}: Aftermath **{{Endn|5d}}: Limited Edition artwork *{{Endn|6}}: [[Echoes of Eternity (Novel)]], Chapter 35 *{{Endn|7}}: [[The End and the Death: Volume I (Novel)]], 2:xx *{{Endn|8}}: [https://web.archive.org/web/20250717161437/https://www.horusheresylegions.com/horus-heresy-legions-shiban-khan-battle-pass/ Horus Heresy Legions] saved page, original link: https://www.horusheresylegions.com/horus-heresy-legions-shiban-khan-battle-pass/ (last accessed 31/7/2025) *{{Endn|9}}: [[Era of Ruin (Anthology)]] **{{Endn|9a}}: [[After the Dawn, the Darkness (Short Story)]] **{{Endn|9b}}: [[Homebound (Short Story)]] [[Category:Characters (Great Crusade)]] [[Category:Characters (Horus Heresy)]] [[Category:Characters (White Scars)]]

Shon'tu.wikitext:
{{Character |Portal ={{IronWarriorsPortal}} |Name ={{PAGENAME}} |Image =ShontuLysander.jpg |Caption =Shon'tu battles his arch-foe [[Darnath Lysander]] |Title = |Homeworld = |Birth =[[Horus Heresy]]-era{{Fn|2c}} |Active Period =[[M31]] — [[M41]] |Death =Reported 999.[[M41]] |Cause of Death =Killed by [[Imperial Fists]] during the [[Battle of the Phalanx]]{{Fn|4}} |Species = [[Human]] [[Astartes]] |Gender =Male |Relatives = [[Perturabo]]
(“Father” via Gene-seed)
[[Iron Warriors]] & Successor warbands
(“Brothers” via Gene-seed) |Occupation ='' *[[Chaos Lord]] of the [[Sons of the Forge]] |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction = '' '' *[[Imperium of Man]] (Formerly) *[[Iron Warriors]] (IV Legion) **[[Sons of the Forge]] *[[Chaos]] **[[Chaos Undivided]] |Notes = }} '''Shon'tu''' is an infamous [[Iron Warriors]] [[Warsmith]] and commander of the warband [[Sons of the Forge]].{{Fn|1}} ===Biography=== Shon'tu was present during the [[Siege of Terra]] and like most within the Iron Warriors, has swore an eternal hatred for their rivals, the [[Imperial Fists]].{{Fn|2c}} Once upon a time he faced with the Imperial Fist [[Darnath Lysander]] (a mere [[Space Marine Scout|Scout]] at that time). Out of mercy for an innocent who was taken hostage by a Shon'tu, Lysander let him escape and long after regretted it.{{Fn|3}} Shon'tu was also responsible for the capture and vicious torture of now-Captain Lysander on [[Malodrax]].He later battled Lysander and the Imperial Fists yet again during the [[Invasion of Taladorn]], where he escaped after being defeated.{{Fn|2c}} Shon'tu later gathered a sizable force of Iron Warriors and other allies in preparation for a breakout of the [[Eye of Terror]] by attacking the nearby [[Imperial Fists]] Starforts of [[Bastion Inviolate]] and [[Endeavour of Will]] in 998.[[M41]]. The attack was led by his personal [[Grand Cruiser]], the ''Ferrous Malice''. Shon'tu consorted with many [[Daemonic]] powers to achieve his aims, binding the creature [[Velthinar]] to his will and making a pact with a band [[Tzeentch]] Daemons known as [[The Dancers]], gaining the creatures services in exchange for a vial of the blood of [[Perturabo]]. Shon'tu hoped to ascend to [[Daemon Prince|Daemonhood]] by killing [[Imperial Fists]] [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] [[Darnath Lysander]] and offering his head to the [[Gods of Chaos]]. Besides consorting heavily with Daemons, Shon'tu has much contempt for his fellow Warsmiths and considers those in his Legion who do not work with the Ruinous Powers to be weak. But despite his preparations, in the end Shon'tu was narrowly defeated in the [[Battle for the Endeavour of Will]], and escaped in a [[Dreadclaw]] to exact his revenge on Lysander on another day.{{Fn|1}} Next, Shon'tu concoted his most audacious plan yet by capturing a [[Space Hulk]] full of [[Tyranids]] and sending it on a collision course with [[Terra]]. However due to the will of the ships captured [[Navigator]], the hulk instead struck the world of [[Drashin]]. Shon'tu's plan was still not without its benefits, as in the [[Infestation on Drashin|ensuing battle]] Imperial Fists [[Chapter Master]] [[Vladimir Pugh]] was killed. In retaliation, nearly the entire Imperial Fists chapter tracked down Shon'tu to his old base of Malodrax, where he had since activated the ancient space station [[Tamunash]]. In the ensuing [[Fall of Malodrax]], Shon'tu was again defeated by a Space Marine coalition.{{Fn|2a}} After the battle, Shon'tu was thought dead. However in 975.[[M41]] Imperial Fists Veteran Sergeant [[Tynon]] was discovered dead on the world of [[Endrion (Planet)|Endrion]] while training [[Cadian]]s. The words ''Shon'tu lives'' were carved into his chest. Later Lysander tracked remnants of the Sons of the Forge to the [[Torricas System]]. However they found only one dead Chaos Marine there, an Iron Warrior whom the Imperium thought had taken command of the warband following Shon'tu's death. He was found disembowelled and chained with the words ''Shon'tu Lives'' smeared in blood next to his corpse.{{Fn|2b}} Shon'tu returned to exact his vengeance on the Imperial Fists in 999.[[M41]]. Allying with the [[Daemon]] [[Be'lakor]], Shon'tu planned to hijack the ''[[Phalanx]]'' and use it to bombard the [[Imperial Palace]] on [[Terra]]. Taking the Imperial Fists by surprise, he found only the battered [[3rd Company (Imperial Fists)|3rd Company]] (later joined by the [[Legion of the Damned]]) defending the vessel. Ultimately the duos' plot was foiled thanks to the intervention of the Legion of the Damned, and the Warsmith was killed by the [[First Company]] squadron of [[Terminator Sergeant]] [[Furan]].{{Fn|4}} However, in [[M42]] [[First Captain|Captain]] [[Darnath Lysander]]'s suspicions were raised by reports of increased [[Iron Warriors]] activity within the [[Cadian Gate]]. Though there is no proof as of yet that Shon'tu is behind it, Lysander may still have an opportunity to claim his revenge, by destroying the [[Warsmith]].{{Fn|5}} ==Sources== *{{Endn|1}}: [[Endeavour of Will (Novella)]],{{cite this}} *2: [[Sentinels of Terra - A Codex: Space Marines Supplement (6th Edition)]]: **{{Endn|2a}}: ''The Fall of Malodrax **{{Endn|2b}}: ''The 3rd Company's Triumph'' **{{Endn|2c}}: ''Lysander's Rise'' *{{Endn|3}}: [[Lysander: The Fist of Dorn (Short Story)]] *{{Endn|4}}: [[Gathering Storm: Fall of Cadia]], ''Chapter 1: The Fate of Phalanx'' *{{Endn|5}}: [https://archive.ph/vo4im Warhammer Community: Darnath Lysander: Captain of the First Company] ''(archived from [https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-gb/articles/ysq9tys7/darnath-lysander-captain-of-the-first-company/ the original] 03 September 2025, last accessed 03 September 2025)'' [[Category:Characters (Horus Heresy)]] [[Category:Characters (Iron Warriors)]] [[fr:Shon'tu]]

Silberman.wikitext:
{{CollegiaTitanicaPortal}}
'''Silberman''' was a [[Princeps]] in the [[Legio Astorum]] [[Titan Legion]], who commanded the [[Warlord Titan]] [[Fortunata Imperiatrix]] during the [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|1a}} 
==History==
During the [[Horus Heresy]], Silberman was beloved by [[Fortunata Imperiatrix]]'s [[Moderatus]] crew of [[Toal]], [[Hazan]] and [[Warden (Moderatus)|Warden]],{{Fn|1a}} who all referred to their [[Princeps]] as '''Father Silberman'''.{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|1b}}{{Fn|1d}} They would all be part of the [[Legio Astorum]] detachment that the Princeps [[Force Leader]] [[Kowley]] led in the [[Battle of Tallarn]]. However disaster struck, when Silberman was killed after being shot in the head by a [[Sniper]], as the Princeps was outside of the Imperiatrix. His crew not only mourned his loss, but also that Silberman had not died in battle, like the Princeps had always wanted to.{{Fn|1a}} Silberman's skull then became one of the items that was traditionally taken from each of Imperiatrix's past Princeps and placed within the [[Warlord Titan]]. These relics were all touched by Imperiatrix's current Princeps, as part of the ritual needed to awaken the war machine. This role fell to the newly graduated Princeps [[Marnoc]], who had to fill the hole his beloved predecessor had left with the Fortunata Imperiatrix's crew. The young Princeps would begin forming a bond with Toal, Hazan and Warden, as the Imperiatrix once more stood beside the other Legio Astorum Titans of Kowley's command.{{Fn|1b}} 

As [[Legio Astorum]]'s [[Titan]]s aided in defending the [[Tallarn]] city of '''Rogsburg''', [[Fortunata Imperiatrix]]'s [[Moderatus]] crew desired to take revenge for Silberman's death.{{Fn|1b}} However despite the number of [[Traitor]]s they slew when Rogsburg was attacked, the [[Imperials]] defending the city were overwhelmed. [[Marnoc]] escaped before the [[Warlord Titan]] was destroyed,{{Fn|1c}} but he later came to the aid of recently arrived [[Ultramarines]] from space, who were securing a dropsite for additional Imperial reinforcements to descend upon. The [[Space Marines]] had come under attack from a group of [[Legio Mortis]] [[Chaos Titans]] and though the Imperiatrix faced certain death, its Moderatus crew agreed with Marnoc's decision to help the Ultramarines. Thanks to their efforts, the Space Marines were saved and the additional reinforcements arrived to aid in destroying the Traitors and the retaking of Rogsburg. However it came at a heavy cost, as the Imperiatrix was destroyed in the battle and only Marnoc and a mortally wounded [[Hazan]] managed to survive its death. As the Princeps carried the Moderatus from the Warlord's wreckage though, Hazan said, "Thank you, father," before he died from his injuries.{{Fn|1d}}

Silvana.wikitext:
{{AdeptaSororitasPortal}}
[[Image:Silvana.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Saint Silvana{{Fn|4}}]]
'''Saint Silvana''' was the leader of the [[Order of the Argent Shroud]]. 

She was one of the first Sisters and during the [[Age of Apostasy]] she traveled to the [[Golden Throne]] alongside [[Alicia Dominica]].{{Fn|2}} In the years after the Apostasy she was among the first Sisters to lead crusades in the name of the [[Emperor]]. Shortly after Dominica founded the [[Order of the Ebon Chalice]], the remaining Sisters of the [[Convent Prioris]] were placed under Silvana's command. However she was struck down before she could ever lead a [[War of Faith]]. The circumstances of her death remain mysterious. Most reliable records say she was poisoned by a [[Death Cult Assassin]] and suggest that the murderer was an agent still loyal to [[Goge Vandire]]. However other accounts state that the [[Alpha Legion]] may have played a part.  The Sisters of the [[Order of the Argent Shroud]] maintain that the assassin had attempted to kill Dominica, but Silvana sacrificed herself.{{Fn|3}} Silvana was an equally mysterious character in life. While her deeds are well known, not a single word of transcript of her speech has survived to this day.{{Fn|3}}

The journal of [[Ecclesiarch]] [[Alexis XXII]] states that her body was laid to rest within the inner sanctum of Convent Prioris, but mysteriously vanished after seven days. Only a silver image of her bones was left, imprinted on her death shroud. This shroud became a relic for which her Order is named.{{Fn|3}}

Simon Van Gelder.wikitext:
{{ImperiumPortal}}
'''Simon Van Gelder''' was a powerful industrialist on [[Tarsis Ultra]].{{Fn|1}}

==History==
{{spoiler|source=Warriors of Ultramar (Novel)}}

When Tarsis Ultra was threatened by a sliver of [[Hive Fleet Leviathan]], many people panicked and fled towards the spaceport.  Van Gelder first encountered the [[Ultramarines]] relief force sent to the planet when his limousine caught a break in the road and caused his luggage to spill off the roof.  [[Space Marine Sergeant|Sergeant]] [[Learchus Abantes]] arrived in time to see Van Gelder berating his driver for the mishap.  Van Gelder seemed oblivious to the fact that his stopped limousine was blocking the highway.

Learchus, already disgusted by the people's cowardice, lifted the limousine out of the road with his bare hands and placed it across the road, ordering the remaining people, including Van Gelder, to turn around and return to the capital city, [[Erebus (City)|Erebus]].

Van Gelder continued to cause trouble as a member of the city's ruling council, angrily objecting to [[Sebastien Montante]]'s decision to demolish several buildings inside the city walls, to deny the incoming [[Tyranids]] cover.  Van Gelder sneered that the Ultramarines' martial valour must have been greatly exaggerated, if they expected the Tyranids to get that far into the city.  Learchus lost his temper and came perilously close to killing Van Gelder.

Van Gelder, too thick-skinned to realize when he had been rebuked, continue to protest Montante's decisions, and Learchus reflected bitterly that he was a prime example that the people of Tarsis Ultra had largely abandoned [[Roboute Guilliman]]'s ideals, since their planet's liberation by the Ultramarines millennia ago.

When the Tyranid invasion began in earnest, Van Gelder decided to flee the planet in his private starship, which he had loaded with almost the entire contents of his estate.  Although all air traffic had been suspended, he had access to override codes allowing him to shut down the air defenses.

His timing could not have been worse.  As his ship lifted off, and he sent the override codes, it crossed paths with a [[Thunderhawk]] gunship carrying a [[Space Marine]] strike force back from an important mission, pursued by a swarm of [[Gargoyle]]s.  Thanks to Van Gelder, the Gargoyles had not been stopped by the city's anti-aircraft guns, and the Thunderhawk took heavy damage before making an emergency landing.  Van Gelder's starship was far too over-laden to evade the Gargoyles, which swarmed over the ship, smashed through the viewports and tore Van Gelder and his crew to pieces.  The ship crashed in a poor quarter of the city, annihilating a warehouse being used by gang leader [[Snowdog]] as a stockpile for illegal goods.

Van Gelder's temporary shutdown of the air defenses also allowed a small flight of [[Harridan]]s to slip into the city, undetected, and plant broods of Gargoyles behind the Imperial lines, which remained dormant until the final battle, when they awoke and allowed the Tyranids to completely encircle the remaining Imperial defenders.

Siphistus.wikitext:
{{DeathGuardPortal}}
'''Plaguelord Siphistus''' was a [[Death Guard]] [[Plague Marine]] who was part of a large [[Chaos Undivided]] warhost{{Fn|1a}} that rampaged across the [[Eastern Fringes]] of the [[Ultima Segmentum]]. The warhost would eventually land on [[Dolumar IV]], a backwater planet, where they built a Chaos temple and summoned the [[Lord of Change]] [[Tarkh'ax]], who would begin to lead them on a new [[Black Crusade]] to strike at Holy [[Terra]]. It would be all for naught however, as after the summoning an [[Eldar]] strikeforce would attack and seal the warhost in a prison; in a cut off path of the [[Webway]]. Siphistus and the warhost would stay in their prison for three thousand years, until the [[heretic]] [[Meyloch Severus]], [[Planetary Governor]] of the now resettled Dolumar IV, completed a Chaos ritual that broke the warhost's prison; and allowed them to materialize on both the [[Imperial Navy]] vessel the [[Enduring Blade]], where the [[Imperium]] and [[Tau Empire]] were conducting peace talks{{Fn|1c}}, and Dolumar IV{{Fn|1d}}. While his Brothers butchered their way through the Enduring Blade{{Fn|1c}}, Siphistus and the warhost that materialized on Dolumar IV, attacked the population there.{{Fn|1d}}

As the Imperium and Tau launched forces onto Dolumar IV to deal with the warhost, Siphistus entered a factory hanger and began to corrupt the newly finished [[Imperial Titan]] [[Imperio Prince-Nebulae Draconis]], to use against the forces attacking them; and to buy Severus more time to complete his ritual that would free the warhost's leader Tarkh'ax. Siphistus strapped himself into the [[Princep]]'s throne and completely corrupted the Titan; and, now calling it the [[Machina Dragon-Bile]], began to activate it. It was during this time that the [[Fire Warrior]] [[La'Kais]] burst into the control room, having fought his way through the forces guarding the Titan, in order to destroy it. The [[Khorne]] [[Chaos Space Marine]], [[Keraz]] and several Plague Marines guarding Siphistus attacked the Fire Warrior, but La'Kais managed to avoid their attacks much Keraz's dismay. In a rage Keraz lost control and began swinging indiscriminately at the Fire Warrior, in his need to spill blood. When he regained himself, Keraz realized he had killed the other [[Chaos Space Marines]] guarding the control room, leaving only Siphistus, strapped in the still activating Titan, alive. At that moment La'Kais, unharmed during Keraz's rampage, emerged and killed him. Siphistus was helpless and could do nothing, as La'Kais dropped the last of several bombs he had planted on the corrupted Titan, on his lap{{Fn|1a}}. Once he was clear La'Kais activated the bombs, killing Siphistus and completely destroying the Machina Dragon-Bile.{{Fn|1e}}

The '''Sire of Doom''' is a [[Dreadblade Knight]].

The Renegade was once the Noble '''Kiro''' of [[House Daitan]] until the [[Mnos Catastrophe]]. In that conflict, the Knights of Daitan, defended [[Imperial]] [[Forge Worlds]] from an invasion by the [[Dark Mechanicum]], but they were overwhelmed and captured. Afterwards the Knights were bound within a [[Soul Forge]] and were tortured in a [[Chaos]] ritual, by having agonizing [[Warp]] currents sent surging through them. One by one the Knights gave into the pain and exploded, which sent their share of the Warp current to the survivors. Soon only Kino was left, but his Knight suit, Sire of Doom, was driven insane as it was flooded with the tortured deaths of the Nobles of House Daitan. The Dark Mechanicum then finished their ritual by sealing the Sire of Doom in its state of utter despair. Now the tortured Knight can see nothing, but the scarred and twisted faces of its Dark Mechanicum captors at every turn, which causes it to lash out at anyone near it. The Knight's Dark Mechanicum masters are well aware of this and in battle they lead the Sire of Doom to where it can cause the most damage.{{Fn|1}}

'''Skane''' was a [[Space Marine Sergeant]] of the [[World Eaters]]' [[8th Company (World Eaters)|8th Company]] during the [[Great Crusade]] and [[Horus Heresy]].{{fn|1a}}

===Biography===
Serving in the 8th Company under [[Khârn]], Skane commanded a [[Destroyer Marine|Destroyer Squad]]{{fn|1a}} and was the one to find his captain on the battlefield of [[Isstvan III]].{{fn|1b}} Like most Destroyer Astartes, he suffered from various ailments caused by the weapons he wielded{{fn|1e}}, and had been fitted with [[Augmetics|augmetic]] vocal cords after an aggressive cancer had destroyed his biological ones.{{fn|1d}} After the battle of [[Armatura]], he supported [[Lotara Sarrin]] when the Flag-Captain challenged [[Delvarus]] for dereliction of duty{{fn|1c}}, and he lost a forearm to the [[Ultramarines]] during the destruction of [[Nuceria]].{{fn|1f}}

Near the end of the Heresy, Skane served aboard the Legion's flagship ''[[Conqueror (Ship)|Conqueror]]'', as it journeyed to take part in the [[Battle for Terra|invasion]] of [[Terra]]. By that time, however, the ''Conqueror'' had fallen under the influence of [[Khorne]], which had led the flagship to become a hostile environment to those aboard it. This led to the rapid depletion of supplies and manpower - chiefly due to the World Eaters losing themselves to mindless rages and then attacking anyone near them. Skane was among the worse to suffer under the ''Conqueror's'' influence and he began to struggle to control his radiation ravaged body. This eventually led him to violently corner the ''Conqueror's'' [[Imperial Army|Captain]] [[Lotara Sarrin]] and tell her they needed to leave the flagship for their own safety. Captain Sarrin agreed with Skane, as he had voiced an opinion that many aboard the ''Conqueror'' now held. However this was not shared with the majority of the World Eaters aboard the ''Conqueror'', who would view this abandonment as a mutiny, so Skane and Sarrin met secretly to begin planning their escape.{{Fn|2}}

They met with others who wished to leave as well and when they had made their final preparations to leave, their group had grown to include fifty World Eaters and over three hundred crew members. Their plan to escape was then put into action, the next time the World Eaters' fleet exited the Warp. As per their plan, Captain Sarrin had secured five shuttles to take the escapees to the Legion [[frigate]] [[Bestiarius]] and one by one they were filled and left the Conqueror behind. Skane and, his fellow World Eater escapee, Captain [[Maruuk]], however, stayed beside Sarrin, who as Captain of the ''Conqueror'' would need to escape aboard the last shuttle, to avoid arising any suspicion.{{Fn|2}}

When they reached the shuttle though, [[Khârn]] confronted them before they could escape and declared them to be traitors. As Khârn then made his approach, Skane charged him and told Captain Sarrin to escape while he held Khârn back. He was no match for Khârn, however, and was soon beaten to the ground, as the last shuttle fled the ''Conqueror''. Khârn then prepared to kill Skane, but the Destroyer Sergeant was content the others had managed to escape. This quickly changed when Sarrin appeared beside Khârn and Skane learned she had betrayed their group and had never planned on leaving. Now helpless and stricken with grief from Sarrin's betrayal, Skane could do nothing as Khârn raised [[Gorechild]] to end his life. However before the blow could land, Sarrin stopped Khârn and stated as Captain of the ''Conqueror'', Skane's death should be her responsibility. With that, she leveled her pistol at Skane's face and shot him through his eye. Shortly afterwards, Sarrin gave the order to destroy the escapees' shuttles and brought an end to their mutiny.{{Fn|2}}

Skulane.wikitext:
{{TanithPortal}}
'''Skulane''' was a [[Trooper]] of the [[Tanith First and Only]]. He served as a special weapons trooper, wielding a [[heavy flamer]].{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|1b}}


==Biography==
At one point during the [[Sabbat Worlds Crusade]], the Tanith First were deployed on the [[Forge World]] of [[Fortis Binary]]. After many months of stalemated trench warfare against the [[Shriven (Chaos Cult)|Shriven]] [[Chaos Cult]], [[Lord High Militant General]] [[Hechtor Dravere]], growing impatient with the lack of progress, ordered the Tanith First and [[Vitrian Dragoons Third|a regiment of]] [[Vitrian Dragoons]] to advance on the enemy position and engage them. During the fighting, the Tanith First was divided in the chaos of the battle. Skulane ended up in a detachment led by [[Colonel]] [[Colm Corbec|Corbec]].{{Fn|1b}}

After working their way through the trench network, the Tanith and Vitrians encountered a series of outbuildings that they found the Shriven had filled with strange, [[Chaos|corrupted]] mechanical drums. Colonel Corbec ordered Skulane to incinerate the contents of each shed, but as he prepared to fire, he was shot in the head by [[Trooper]] [[Drayl]], who had been corrupted by a Chaos artefact in the trenches. To make matters worse, the Tanith were forced to blow up Skulane's body with [[grenade]]s, as his heavy flamer was writhing out of control on the ground where he had dropped it.{{Fn|1b}}

Solana (Historitor).wikitext:
{{AdeptusMechanicusPortal}}
'''Solana''' is a founding member of the [[Logos Historica Verita]], alongside [[Deven Mudire]], [[Fabian Guelphrain]] and [[Theodore Viablo]].{{Fn|1a}}
==History==
Solana is a [[Martian]] who [[Lord Regent]] [[Roboute Guilliman]] selected to join the [[Logos Historica Verita]]; though frequently assumed by the uninitiated, Solana is not a [[Tech-Priest]], as she often points out {{Fn|1b}}. The Martian and [[Deven Mudire]] were among the first selected to join the Logos Historica Verita, alongside a third historitor named [[Thiennes]]. Thiennes would however be removed for displeasing Guilliman and his fall from grace greatly impacted both Solana and Deven {{Cite This}}. The two would later be joined by [[Fabian Guelphrain]], a [[Terran]] [[Adept]], who was from a lower social strata. While Solana treated Fabian with kindness and answered any questions he had, the aristocrat Mudire treated the commoner Adept with disdain. Guilliman later brought the three of them to meet with [[Magos Dominus|Archmagos Dominus]] [[Belisarius Cawl]] aboard his [[Ark Mechanicus]] [[Zar-Quaesitor]]. This was Fabian's first off-world experience and Solana took the time to ease his worry. As they talked, the Martian told Fabian that she was excited to meet Cawl, whose work was an inspiration to her, despite the fact that many within the [[Adeptus Mechanicus]] decried him as a [[Heretek]]{{Fn|1b}}. On the Zar-Quaesitor{{Fn|1c}}, the three historitors would witness Cawl's unveiling of the [[Primaris Space Marines]]{{Fn|1d}}. 

Soon afterwards, the [[Indomitus Crusade]] began and the three historitors were assigned to [[Lord Commander of the Imperium|Lord Commander]] [[Guilliman]]'s [[Fleet Primus]], as it prepared to leave [[Terra]]. There, they were joined by a fourth historitor, [[Theodore Viablo]]. The four would be given tasks to ascertain their talent by compiling historical facts in order to establish a true history of the [[Imperium]]. If found to be of sufficient quality, their works would be given to Roboute Guilliman's [[Fleetmaster]]s to read. Solana's work would be accepted by the [[Primarch]]{{Fn|1e}}.     

The four would then serve beside each for several years in Fleet Primus, training many other members of the [[Logos Historica Verita]] and collating a history of the Imperium since the end of the [[Horus Heresy]]{{Fn|1e}}. However after witnessing the [[Founding]] ceremony of the [[Void Sabres]], the 104th [[Ultima Founding]] they had witnessed together, the founding members were finally separated. On the orders of [[Roboute Guilliman]], they were given new duties that sent them away from Fleet Primus - all save for Viablo who was to remain as Guilliman's personal chronicler. Solana herself was charged with traveling to the [[Adeptus Mechanicus]]' [[Forge Worlds]], where she would serve as a herald for the Logos Historica Verita. It would then be several years, before the four founding members were reunited again.{{Fn|2}}

Solathen.wikitext:
{{EmperorsChildrenPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was a member of the [[Emperor's Children]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]] and served in [[Squad Nasicae]] during the [[Great Crusade]]. His squad was later chosen by their [[Primarch]] [[Fulgrim]], to go to [[Isstvan III]] in order to suppress a revolt by the [[Planetary Governor]] [[Vardus Praal]] and were among the first wave to land upon the planet.{{Fn|1a}} 

The squad later aided [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] [[Lucius (Emperor's Children)|Lucius]]{{Fn|1a}} in attacking Praal's bodyguard, which allowed Lucius to kill the corrupted Governor{{Fn|1b}}. Soon after Praal's death however, [[Warmaster]] [[Horus]] revealed his [[Horus Heresy|treachery]] and unleashed several [[Virus Bomb]]s onto Isstvan III; beginning the [[Battle of Isstvan III|purging]] of the [[Sons of Horus]], [[Emperor's Children]], [[Death Guard]] and [[World Eaters]] Legions, of those deemed too loyal to the [[Emperor]]{{Fn|1c}}.

Solathen and the few remaining members of his squadron, were able to survive both the Virus Bombs and the firestorm that followed, and later regrouped with other surviving [[Loyalist]]s in the '''Precentor’s Palace'''. As a result, the Palace became a target for the [[Traitor]]s as they sought to kill any surviving Loyalists and Solathen defended it from countless attacks{{Fn|1d}}. During one such attack, traitorous members of the Emperor's Children, led by [[Lord Commander]] [[Eidolon]], managed to breach the Palace's defenses; catching the Loyalists by surprise. During the attack, Solathen led a group of Loyalists in order to push the Traitors back, when Captain [[Saul Tarvitz]] contacted him; to ask Solathen to bring any Emperor's Children near him to the Captain's location, so they could launch an ambush on the Traitors. However, when Solathen and his Loyalist group located Tarvitz, they found the Captain engaged in a losing duel with Lucius. When Tarvitz saw Solathen and his group, he told them to fire upon Lucius, who had betrayed the Loyalists and had allowed the Traitors into the Palace, in exchange for being allowed to rejoin his Legion. Once he heard this, Solathen and the Loyalist Emperor's Children fired upon Lucius and wounded him, but they were unable to stop the traitor from escaping. With the Captain saved, Solathen and his group of Loyalists joined Tarvitz in launching an ambush on Eidolon and the Traitorous Emperor's Children{{Fn|1e}}, which forced them to retreat from the Palace. Afterwards, he would continue to be a great aid to the Loyalists, until the end finally came; when the Traitors ended their attacks and began returning to their ships in orbit. When his surviving forces were completely evacuated, Horus gave the order to begin an orbital bombardment on Isstvan III, to ensure the Loyalists were killed. In the Precentor's Palace, Solathen was huddled with Tarvitz, and the hundred surviving Loyalists that still remained, when he asked the Captain if their efforts had hurt the Traitors. As the bombardment began to strike Isstvan III's surface, Tarvitz assured Solathen that they had, just before the Palace suffered a direct hit and was destroyed.{{Fn|1f}}

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an [[Inquisitor]] of the [[Ordo Hereticus]] active in the [[Calixis Sector]].{{Fn|1}}

Originally an [[Interrogator]] serving [[Rykehuss]], he broke with the Witch Finder after his own promotion. Soldevan believes that knowledge is the key to protecting humanity, which clashed with the [[Puritan]]'s views. He has quickly turned [[Radical]], believing that the [[Warp]] is a source of knowledge and power and that a man of sufficient intelligence can harness it. Thus he seeks to open a pathway to the Warp and seek out the consciousness that dwells within, bargaining with them for the power he needs to combat the enemies of [[mankind]]. This has led Soldevan to collect many dark [[Chaos]] artefacts. Somewhere during the process, he has lost his sanity.{{Fn|1}}

Solinus.wikitext:
{{UltramarinesPortal}}
'''Solinus''' is a [[Space Marine Sergeant]] from the [[Ultramarines]] [[2nd Company (Ultramarines)|2nd Company]], under [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] [[Cato Sicarius]].  His [[Tactical Squad]], nicknamed "The Indomitable," received [[Victorex Maxima]] honours during the retaking of [[Fort Telrendar]], when they were the first into the breach after Sicarius.{{Fn|1a}}

==History==
===Black Reach===
During the [[Assault on Black Reach]] in 855 [[M41]]{{Fn|1b}}, The Indomitable were deployed to [[Black Reach]] with the rest of the Second Company against [[Waaagh!]] [[Zanzag]].  They had the honour of being the first squad to follow Sicarius during the initial [[drop pod]] assault against the [[Ork]]s who were about to overrun Ghospora Hive, and the subsequent assault on Zanzag's base.{{Fn|2a}}{{Fn|2b}}

Among the 2nd Company's sergeants, Solinus was one of those who leaned towards caution and were wary of what some called their Captain's recklessness.{{Fn|2c}}

===Espandor===
During the attack of the [[Bloodborn]] on [[Ultramar]], in 854999.M41{{Fn|1b}}, the 2nd Company was deployed to [[Espandor]].{{Fn|3}}

Sollon.wikitext:
{{ImperialFistsPortal}}
'''Sollon''' was a venerable [[Codicier]] in the [[Imperial Fists]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]] who, on the orders of his [[Primarch]] [[Dorn]], was imprisoned with the Legion's other [[Librarian]]s aboard the [[Phalanx]], following the [[Edict of Nikaea]]. The Librarians would remain there, even after the [[Horus Heresy]] began{{fn|1a}}, until the [[Solar War]] when Dorn unleashed them to aid in defending the Phalanx, from a [[Daemonic]] invasion led by the Daemon [[Samus]].{{fn|1b}}

Solomon Haarlock.wikitext:
{{ImperiumPortal}}
'''Solomon Haarlock''' was a [[Rogue Trader]], who was a scion of [[House Haarlock]].{{Fn|1}} 
==History==
He successfully charted the area of space that would become known as [[Calixis Sector]], circa 760.[[M36]]. Some say Solomon later strayed [[Koronus Expanse|beyond]] what would become known as the [[Koronus Passage]] [[Warp Route]].{{Fn|1}}
